To conceptualize these dynamics, we propose a Layered Conversion Model, in which social capital functions as latent potential, community empowerment serves as the conversion mechanism, and infrastructure constitutes the payoff ceiling. This model not only extends Sen’s capability approach but also offers a replicable analytical framework for evaluating the effectiveness of Indonesia’s village fund programmes. Our findings underscore the need to integrate empowerment strategies with infrastructure investment to strengthen pathways toward sustainable rural economic independence.

title: Multilevel Analysis: The Impact of Conceptual Social Capital on Stunting in Children Under Five in Tulungagung Regency, East Java, Indonesia
authors: Ayun Widya Rizki; Didik Gunawan Tamtomo; Bhisma Murti
venue: Journal of Maternal and Child Health
abstract: Background: Stunted children have inadequate nutritional intake, which may affect neural cell maturation and make them vulnerable to developmental delays, such as delayed motor develop­ment, lower cognitive ability, and slower social responses. Social capital can serve as a stimulatory resource within a community. The concept of social capital was initially understood as a form of trust that people place in their community and in individuals as members of that commu­nity. This study aimed to estimate the association of social capital with stunting among children under five years of age while accounting for contextual effects at the integrated community health post (posyandu) level. Subjects and Method: This was an analytical cross-sectional study. The target population comprised children aged 6–59 months with stunting. The sample consisted of 100 stunted children aged 6–59 months and their mothers, and 100 non-stunted children aged 6–59 months and their mothers, randomly selected from the working areas of Sumbergempol, Tunggangri, and Rejotangan Primary Health Centers in Tulungagung Regency, East Java, Indonesia. The dependent variable was stunting. The independent variables were education, income, and social capital. The data were analyzed using multiple multilevel logistic regression, with posyandu as the second-level unit. Results: Multilevel multiple logistic regression analysis showed that the risk of stunting among children under five was lower among those whose mothers had higher education (≥senior high school) (b= −1.17; 95% CI = −2.09 to −0.24; p= 0.013), whose parents had higher income (≥ IDR 1,500,000/month) (b= −0.94; 95% CI= −1.59 to −0.28; p= 0.013), and who lived in communities with high social capital (b= −0.69; 95% CI= −1.34 to −0.03; p= 0.039). The analysis indicated a substantial contextual effect of factors at the posyandu level within villages on stunting among children under five (ICC = 8.90%). Conclusion: The risk of stunting among children under five was lower among children whose mothers had higher education (≥ senior high school), whose parents had higher income (≥ IDR 1,500,000/month), and who lived in communities with high social capital.

title: Association between individual-level social capital and metabolic syndrome among middle-aged community dwellers in rural Vietnam
authors: Aki Yazawa; Ichiro I. Kawachi; Thuy Thi Phuong Pham; Chau Que Nguyen; Aoi Ito; Danh Cong Phan
abstract: Introduction While social capital is linked to various health outcomes, its association with metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains underexplored, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) facing rising cardiovascular disease burdens. This study examines the association between social capital and MetS in Vietnam, a country undergoing rapid epidemiological and nutritional transitions. Research design and methods Data were collected from 2825 participants in the baseline survey of the Khánh Hòa Cardiovascular Study, a prospective cohort study of local residents aged 40–60 years in the Khánh Hòa province, Vietnam. Poisson regression models with robust variance estimator were used to assess the association between cognitive (low, middle or high) and structural social capital (yes or no) and MetS, as well as its individual components, with results stratified by sex. Results We found that 34.7% of male and 36.8% of female participants had MetS. Among female participants, those with high cognitive social capital had a lower likelihood of MetS compared with those with low cognitive social capital (prevalence ratio (PR)=0.84, 95% CI 0.72 to 0.97), while no significant association was observed among male participants. Regarding structural social capital, no association with MetS was observed in either sex. In analyses of individual MetS components, high cognitive social capital was associated with a lower prevalence of elevated blood pressure among females (PR=0.92, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.00). Conclusions Cognitive social capital was associated with lower prevalence of MetS among women in rural Vietnam. Further longitudinal studies are warranted to clarify causal pathways. Social capital may be important to consider in cardiometabolic health efforts in LMICs undergoing rapid socioeconomic change.

title: Social Capital, Maternal Autonomy, and the Utilization of Maternal and Child Healthcare Services in West Bengal: Evidence from NFHS-5
authors: Ramananda Roy
venue: International Journal of Financial Management and Economics
abstract: Background: Despite significant improvements in health infrastructure, maternal and child health (MCH) indicators in India exhibit substantial regional heterogeneity. West Bengal, a state with high population density and complex socio-cultural dynamics, presents a critical case for examining the non-medical determinants of health service utilisation. This study investigates the influence of social capital and maternal autonomy on the utilisation of MCH services. Methods: Secondary data analysis was conducted using the National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5, 2019-21) unit-level data for West Bengal. The study sample comprised 22,462 women aged 15-49 years. Dependent variables included antenatal care (ANC) visits, institutional delivery, postnatal care (PNC), and child immunisation. Independent variables included indices of social capital (group membership, media exposure) and maternal autonomy (decision-making power). Binary logistic regression models were employed to estimate associations, controlling for socio-demographic covariates. Results: The analysis indicates that 68.5% of women received full ANC, and 89.3% of births occurred in institutions. Maternal autonomy showed a strong positive association with institutional delivery (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR]: 1.45; 95% CI: 1.32-1.59) and full immunisation (AOR: 1.38; 95% CI: 1.25-1.52). Social capital, particularly membership in self-help groups and exposure to mass media, significantly predicted PNC utilisation (AOR: 1.29; 95% CI: 1.15-1.44). Conclusion: Both individual agency (autonomy) and community resources (social capital) are critical drivers of MCH service utilisation in West Bengal. Policy interventions must move beyond infrastructure development to focus on women's empowerment and community network strengthening to achieve Sustainable Development Goal 3.

title: Workplace social capital and self-rated health among nursery school teachers in Japan: a nationwide cross-sectional study
authors: Tomosa MINE; Satoshi Tsuboi; Yumi Yodogawa; Masahiro Imafuku; 弘子 猪熊; Junko Minowa
abstract: Introduction: Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) professionals, such as nursery school teachers in Japan, are essential for children's development but face substantial physical and emotional demands that may affect their health. In recent years, workplace social capital (WSC)-defined as trust, reciprocity, and cooperative relationships within the workplace-has been recognized as an important determinant of employee health. Although associations between WSC and health outcomes have been reported in several occupational groups, little is known about its role among ECCE professionals. This study investigated the relationship between WSC and self-rated health (SRH) among Japanese nursery school teachers caring for children under 3 years of age. Methods: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study from February to May 2024, targeting 5,000 randomly selected childcare facilities across Japan. Self-administered questionnaires collected data on demographics, work-hours-related conditions, WSC, and SRH. SRH was assessed using a single-item measure and dichotomized into "good" and "poor." WSC was measured using the Japanese version of the Finnish Public Sector Study (FPSS) scale and categorized into four groups. Logistic regression models estimated crude and adjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Of 2,470 valid responses, 10.4% reported poor SRH. Compared with the very high WSC group, participants in the very low WSC group had significantly higher odds of poor SRH (adjusted OR = 5.60; 95% CI: 3.24-9.70). This association remained significant after adjusting for work-hours-related conditions. Notably, additional adjustment for taking daily rest breaks attenuated the association (adjusted OR = 4.43; 95% CI: 2.40-7.00). Conclusion: This study provides the first nationwide evidence linking WSC with SRH among Japanese nursery school teachers. Lower WSC was strongly associated with poor SRH, independent of work-hours-related conditions. Supportive and cohesive workplace relationships may enhance perceived health and facilitate effective recovery from fatigue, underscoring their importance in ECCE settings.

title: Longitudinal Study on the Relationship Between Club Participation Tendency and Subjective Social Capital and Psychological Distress Among University Students
authors: Michimasa Haga; Hideshi Kodaira; Shinji Nakamura; Yoshihiko Yamazaki; Katsunori Kondo
abstract: Abstract This study investigated the longitudinal associations among club participation tendency, changes in subjective social capital, and psychological distress in university students. Panel data were collected from students at a private university in Japan, spanning their first to fourth academic years. Latent growth curve modeling yielded four principal findings. First, participation tendency in sports clubs was negatively associated with the slope of psychological distress. Second, increases in subjective social capital were likewise negatively associated with the slope of psychological distress. Third, participation in volunteer clubs, sports clubs, and multiple club types was positively related to the slope of subjective social capital. Fourth, although club participation tendency was significantly associated with changes in subjective social capital, and changes in subjective social capital were significantly associated with changes in psychological distress, the indirect effect via changes in subjective social capital was not statistically significant. This may be partly due to the fact that subjective social capital was not assessed across different relational domains, potentially obscuring domain‐specific pathways linking club participation tendency to psychological distress. These findings suggest that club participation tendency and subjective social capital may be important factors contributing to improvements in psychological adjustment among university students.

title: Agricultural Empowerment and Social Capital Transformation among Marginalized Indigenous Communities: Evidence from the Suku Anak Dalam of Indonesia
authors: Isyaturriyadhah Isyaturriyadhah; Yonariza Yonariza
venue: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences
abstract: Empirical quantitative evidence on social capital dynamics in nomadic/semi–nomadic Indigenous communities is limited, specifically in agricultural empowerment programs. Therefore, this study aims to present descriptive evidence of changes in important dimensions of social capital, trust, networks, reciprocity, shared values, and solidarity among Suku Anak Dalam (SAD) community in Jambi Province, Indonesia, after willing participation in government–supported agricultural empowerment programs. Data collection was conducted among 93 participants diagnosed with SAD based on a census–based survey. The measurement was carried out using a five–point Likert–scale scoring system. Semi–structured interviews with government officials and local experts were performed to provide a context for the quantitative design. The results showed that there were observable increases in all the dimensions of social capital, with the greatest relative gains observed in the dimensions of trust and reciprocity. Furthermore, patterns of association were described between program participation and the perceived social capital outcomes rather than causal effects. This context–specific work offered empirical data of an underserved Indigenous population and identified the connection of agricultural empowerment programs to social capital enhancement among marginalized rural population. The results were conservative to policymakers and development practitioners, designing contextualized empowerment interventions. Keywords: Agricultural empowerment, community dynamics, social capital reciprocity, social trust .

title: How STEM social capital shapes secondary school students’ STEM aspirations: the roles of STEM expectations and mathematics competency
authors: Shiyu Xu; Jiateng Zhou; Yulian Cao
abstract: Secondary students’ STEM aspirations strongly predict later STEM degrees and careers. Understanding how these aspirations are shaped is therefore critical. Family and school contexts are widely recognized as important influences, but the specific pathways through which these influences operate remain underexplored. Grounded in science capital theory, this study conceptualizes STEM social capital in terms of parental STEM occupations and homeroom teachers’ STEM backgrounds, and examines how these factors relate to Chinese secondary school students’ STEM aspirations, the mediating pathways involved, and heterogeneity across sex and urban–rural contexts. Using data from the 2014–2015 follow-up wave of the nationally representative longitudinal data from the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS), this study analyzed a restricted sample of 5,123 eighth-grade students in 122 classrooms across 61 schools. The sample was restricted to schools with random classroom assignment in seventh grade and no performance-based reshuffling in eighth grade to better identify homeroom teacher effects. Balance checks suggest that the restricted analytical sample is broadly comparable to excluded cases on most school-level characteristics, although it includes fewer rural and socioeconomically disadvantaged schools and students. Linear probability models with school fixed effects were estimated while controlling for student, family, and classroom characteristics, followed by mediation and heterogeneity analyses. The results showed that Chinese secondary school students with greater STEM social capital were more likely to report STEM aspirations. Parental STEM occupations influenced aspirations through STEM expectations, with students’ perceived parental STEM expectations exerting a stronger mediating effect. Homeroom teachers’ STEM backgrounds were linked to aspirations through mathematics competency, with mathematics performance showing a slightly stronger mediating effect than students’ self-assessment of mathematics competency. Heterogeneity analyses showed that parental STEM occupations, particularly fathers’ STEM occupations, were more strongly associated with girls’ STEM aspirations, whereas homeroom teachers’ STEM backgrounds were more strongly associated with boys’ STEM aspirations. In addition, parental STEM occupations were significant only in urban schools, whereas homeroom teachers’ STEM backgrounds were more pronounced in rural schools. This study provides a relational and contextually grounded account of how multiple sources of STEM social capital shape secondary school students’ STEM aspirations in the Chinese context. By revealing family- and school-based pathways, this study provides practical guidance and insights for parents, teachers, and policymakers on how to support students’ STEM aspirations in China and other similar educational contexts.

title: Empowering Bangladeshi women entrepreneurs as food service providers: bridging innovation, social capital, knowledge, performance, and sustainable development
authors: Md.  Tariqul Islam; Uma Pandey; Jeetesh Kumar
abstract: The present study examined the relationship between Bangladeshi women's food service providers' entrepreneurial innovations, social capital, entrepreneurial knowledge, entrepreneurial performance, entrepreneurial success, and sustainable development goal (SDGs) 5 (gender equality) and 8 (decent work and economic growth). This study is a quantitative cross-sectional study that was conducted by surveying 196 Bangladeshi women food service providers. The data was collected through a purposive sampling technique. The findings of this study revealed that Bangladeshi women's homemade food service providers' entrepreneurial innovations, social capital, and entrepreneurial knowledge positively influence their entrepreneurial performance and success. In addition, entrepreneurial success positively impacts achieving SDGs 5 and 8. The result highlights that successful food service businesses operated by Bangladeshi women directly contribute to achieving the country's sustainable development goal. This study contributes both theoretically and practically. Theoretically, the study provides a research framework to emphasise what factors impact women's entrepreneurial success and how successful women entrepreneurs can contribute to achieving the sustainable development goal. Practically, this study provides several implications for the stakeholders of the respective industry.

title: Social Capital and Integration Patterns among Korean Diaspora Residents in Korea: Differential Effects by Diaspora Type and Length of Residence
authors: Minyi Yoo
abstract: 본 연구는 국내 거주 동포의 사회자본이 통합성과에 미치는 영향이 동포유형(중국동포·고려인)과 체류기간에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지를 분석하였다. 「2025년 국내 거주 동포 실태조사」 자료를 활용하여 사회자본을 인지적 결속형·행동적 결속형·연계형의 3차원으로 구분하고, 통합성과를 객관통합(소득·자산), 주관통합(소속감·삶의 만족도), 정주의사로 나누어 검토하였다. 분석은 위계적 회귀분석, 민족 다집단 계수차 검정, 2차 폴리노미얼 궤적분석의 세 단계로 구성하였다. 분석 결과, 첫째, 주관통합에서는 인지적 결속형의 정(+)효과, 행동적 결속형의 부(-)효과, 연계형의 정(+)효과가 비교적 공통적으로 확인되었다. 둘째, 객관통합에서는 고려인에게서 인지적 결속형 사회자본의 효과가 더 크게 나타나, 사회자본이 언어자본과 제도적 자원의 상대적 제약을 보완하는 대리 자원으로 기능할 가능성이 확인되었다. 셋째, 체류기간의 효과는 중국동포에서 소득·자산·소속감·정주의사에 대해 역U자형으로 나타난 반면, 고려인에서는 뚜렷한 시간추세가 확인되지 않았다. 넷째, 정주의사는 사회자본보다 비자변경경험, 주거안정, 학력 등 구조적·제도적 요인의 영향을 더 크게 받는 것으로 나타났다. 이러한 결과는 국내 거주 동포의 통합이 단일한 경로를 따르지 않으며, 사회자본의 유형, 동포유형, 체류단계, 제도적 조건이 결합하는 조건부 과정임을 보여준다. 따라서 동포 통합정책은 재외동포라는 단일 범주를 전제로 한 획일적 지원에서 벗어나, 집단별·단계별·특성별 차이를 반영한 맞춤형 정책설계로 전환될 필요가 있다.

title: Financial Literacy, Psychological Capital and Social Capital on Entrepreneurial of Organic Rice Farmers in Trawas Sub District, Mojokerto District
authors: Sabil Fajar Fath; Abdul Wahib Muhaimin; Silvana Maulidah
abstract: Organic agricultural entrepreneurship plays a crucial role in enhancing rural livelihoods and promoting sustainable development. However, the success of farmers in developing entrepreneurial capacity is often influenced by various internal and external factors, such as financial literacy, psychological resilience, and social networks. Understanding how these factors interact is essential to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of organic rice farming communities. This study examines the influence of financial literacy, psychological capital, and social capital on entrepreneurship of organic rice farmers in Trawas District, Mojokerto Regency, East Java Province. Objective of this study is to analyze how the interaction between the four variables can affect the entrepreneurial ability of farmers. The research method was conducted through a survey on 100 organic rice farmers using purposive sampling technique. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling Generalized Structured Component Analysis (SEM GSCA). The results of the analysis show that financial literacy contributes significantly to entrepreneurship, with an influence of 30%. In addition, psychological capital and social capital contribute 16.5% and 35.2% respectively to entrepreneurship development. Financial literacy not only has a direct impact on entrepreneurship, but also strengthens psychological capital and social capital which play an important role in facing entrepreneurial challenges. However, the effect of financial literacy on entrepreneurship through these two mediating variables is not directly significant.

title: Cognitive and structural social capital in farmers’ adoption of plant protection drone technology: evidence from Henan Province, China
authors: Liu Xinyi; Yutian Zhang; Zhao Kai
abstract: Introduction Exploring the influence of social capital on farmers’ adoption of plant protection drone technology is crucial for guiding mechanized plant protection practices and achieving high-quality agricultural development. Methods Based on survey data from farmers in Henan Province in 2024, this study employs an ordered probit model to empirically investigate the impact of social capital on farmers’ adoption of plant protection drone technology and its underlying mechanisms. Results and discussion Baseline regression results indicate that social capital positively influences farmers’ adoption of plant protection drone technology, with cognitive social capital playing a more significant role than structural social capital. Mechanism analysis reveals that social capital affects adoption behavior by improving farmers’ access to credit and non-farm employment opportunities. Heterogeneity analysis shows that social capital’s influence is stronger among households with joint male–female decision-making, smallholder farmers, and those engaged in single-grain cropping, compared to male-dominated decision-making households, large-scale farmers, and those practicing diversified cropping. The study concludes with recommendations to enhance the promotion of plant protection drone technology and to recognize the role of social capital in shaping farmers’ technology adoption decisions.

title: The mediating role of health-related behaviors between social capital and primary healthcare physicians’ health-related quality of life
authors: Zonghao Wu; Zhuoqi Gu; Yukun Wei; Yuankai Huang; Ennan Wang
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the correlation between social capital and physicians' health-related quality of life(HRQoL) in primary healthcare institutions. Simultaneously, we examined the mediating role of health-related behaviors in the process. Data was obtained from a nationwide cross-sectional survey conducted in 2021. Demographic characteristics and health-related behaviors were collected by a self-administered questionnaire. We used the social capital of healthcare organizations reported by employees (SOCAPO-E) scale to measure the social capital and the EuroQol-five dimension-five level (EQ-5D-5L) to measure physicians' HRQoL. The Tobit model was performed to evaluate the association between social capital and HRQoL. Spearman's test was applied to investigate the relationship between social capital, health-related behaviors and HRQoL. A bootstrap approach was used to assess the mediating effect of health-related behaviors. The regression results showed that social capital (β = 0.605, p<0.001) was significantly and positively associated with physicians' HRQoL. Spearman's correlation analysis showed that social capital was positively correlated with health-related behaviors (r = 0.211, p < 0.01), health-related behaviors were positively correlated with HRQoL (r = 0.134, p < 0.01), and social capital was positively correlated with HRQoL (r = 0.253, p < 0.01). Health-related behaviors moderately mediated the relationship between social capital and HRQoL (BootSE = 0.006, BootCI=[0.005,0.030]). Social capital not only directly affected physicians' HRQoL, but also indirectly affected HRQoL through health-related behaviors. Our findings suggested that future intervention measures could complement the strengthening of social capital with health behavior promotion programs to achieve more comprehensive health improvements.

title: Knowledge network road: an analysis of short-video use among the disabled communities from a social capital integration perspective
authors: Xiaoping Wu; Yuling Fang; Hongfeng Zhou
abstract: Purpose This study examines how short-video use is associated with the subjective social integration of people with disabilities. It conceptualises social integration across three dimensions – self-integration, relational integration and emotional integration – and investigates the differentiated roles of duration of use, content preferences and motivations for use. Drawing on social capital and intellectual capital perspectives, the study further develops a knowledge-network pathway to explain how platform-mediated relationships and information may be converted into knowledge, relational and institutional-action capabilities. Design/methodology/approach The study employed a cross-sectional questionnaire survey. A questionnaire-based quantitative study in Shanghai, with 468 valid responses and an analytical sample of 344 respondents who had used short-video applications. Respondents with visual and hearing disabilities constituted the majority of the sample. The questionnaire measured duration of use, content preferences, motivations for use and three dimensions of subjective social integration. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple-response analysis, cross-tabulated Pearson chi-square tests, two-tailed Spearman's rank-order correlations and simultaneous-entry ordinary least squares regression. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple-response analysis, cross-tabulated Pearson chi-square tests, two-tailed Spearman's rank-order correlations and simultaneous-entry ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. It should be noted that this study employs OLS regression rather than structural equation modelling (SEM), given that the primary aim is to examine the direct associations between specific usage behaviours and each dimension of social integration, rather than to test a comprehensive structural model with latent constructs and mediation pathways. Findings Duration of short-video use was not significantly associated with overall, relational or emotional integration, although it was weakly and positively correlated with self-integration and its subdimensions of self-identity and participatory behaviour. Content preferences exhibited differentiated associations: preferences for humorous narratives, talent-related content and everyday-life content were positively associated with self-integration, while everyday-life, news and humorous content were associated with relational integration. Motivations for use also operated in different directions. Entertainment and relaxation, socialising and broadening one's horizons were positively associated with particular dimensions of integration, whereas purposeless browsing or passing time was negatively associated with self-integration and relational integration. The models had modest explanatory power, suggesting that what people watch and why they use short-video platforms may be more relevant to social integration than duration of use alone. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional and self-reported data do not permit causal inference. The sample was restricted to Shanghai, recruited through social organisations and predominantly comprised respondents with visual or hearing disabilities. The findings therefore cannot be directly generalised to non-users, other regions or people with intellectual, psychosocial or multiple disabilities. The modest explanatory power of the models also indicates that social integration is shaped by factors beyond platform use. Future research should employ stratified or quota sampling, longitudinal and experimental designs, digital trace data and digital ethnography, together with accessible and participatory research procedures adapted to different disability groups. Practical implications Public authorities, platform companies, rehabilitation professionals, welfare programme designers and disability organisations should establish sustained collaborative mechanisms centred on accessible platform use, actionable information, relational support, emotional safety and institutional connections. Platform accessibility should move beyond enabling initial access towards ensuring sustained, equitable and safe participation. Disability-related information should also be made searchable, credible and convertible into rehabilitation, employment, welfare and rights-related action. Social implications The findings challenge technologically deterministic assumptions that platform access, visibility or prolonged use automatically produces empowerment and social integration. Responsibility for digital inclusion should not be transferred to people with disabilities themselves. Meaningful integration requires the conversion of visibility into respect, information into actionable knowledge and institutional resources, and online interaction into relationships grounded in trust. It therefore depends on coordinated efforts to address inaccessible design, algorithmic discrimination, online stigma and exclusionary offline conditions. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature in three respects. Firstly, it develops a multidimensional and subjectively oriented framework that distinguishes among self-integration, relational integration and emotional integration in short-video environments. Secondly, it demonstrates the differentiated associations of usage duration, content preferences and motivations with social integration, thereby moving beyond binary measures of platform access. Thirdly, it conceptualises short-video platforms as knowledge-network infrastructures through which bonding, bridging and linking social capital may be converted into individual intellectual capital. This extends intellectual capital research beyond organisational knowledge management to encompass marginalised groups, public value and social integration in a platformised society.

title: A Latent Profile Analysis of Coping Strategies among Adolescent Cyberbullying Victims: Comparing the Roles of Online and Offline Social Capital
authors: Keyu Chen; Qiqi Chen
abstract: Abstract Cyberbullying victimization among adolescents is an escalating concern, necessitating deeper insights into coping strategies. This study aims to uncover distinct patterns of coping strategies and to examine how prior cyber-victimization, private information disclosure (self-disclosure, disclosure perpetration, disclosure victimization), and social capital (online and offline) relate to these empirically derived profiles. A sample of 1,716 Chinese secondary students (mean age = 14.62 years; 44.5% male) from public ( n = 1,132) and vocational ( n = 584) schools completed the survey. Using latent profile analysis (LPA), we identified three distinct profiles of coping strategies: (1) Maladaptive and Avoidant , (2) Moderate and Cognitive-Reframing , and (3) High Engagement and Flexible . R3STEP Multinomial Logistic Regression results showed that adolescents in the Maladaptive and Avoidant group had the highest scores in disclosure of private information, cyberbullying victimization, and online social capital, alongside the lowest scores in offline social capital. Adolescents in the Moderate and Cognitive-Reframing group reported the highest levels of offline social capital. Those in the High Engagement and Flexible group reported the lowest scores of all adversities. This profiling offers significant advantages over traditional typologies by providing a data-driven method for identifying coping profiles and capturing the dynamic interactions of multiple factors within individuals. This research provides valuable insights for designing more targeted interventions that address the specific needs of each group, particularly for adolescents with avoidant tendencies.

title: The Effect of Digital Literacy on Social Capital Among Older Adults: Dual Mediating Roles of Social Participation and Social Networks
authors: Eun Ju Jung; Kyoung Ri Han
abstract: 본 연구는 초고령사회 진입에 따라 노년기의 이질성을 고려한 관점에서 65세 이상 74세 이하의 전기노인을 대상으로 디지털 리터러시가 사회자본에 미치는 영향과 사회활동 및 사회적 관계망의 순차적 이중매개효과를 검증하는 데 목적이 있다. 이를 위해 D광역시에 거주하는 전기노인 328명을 대상으로 편의표집에 의한 설문조사를 실시하였으며, 수집된 자료는 SPSS 25.0과 Hayes(2017)의PROCESS macro Model 6을 활용하여 분석하였다. 연구 결과, 전기노인의 디지털 리터러시는 사회자본에 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 또한 디지털 리터러시와 사회자본 간의 관계에서 사회활동과 사회적 관계망은 각각 유의한 매개효과를 나타냈으며, 사회활동과 사회적 관계망을 순차적으로 거치는 이중매개효과 역시 통계적으로 유의한 것으로 확인되었다. 이러한 결과는 노인의 사회자본 증진을 위해 디지털 역량 강화와 함께 사회참여 기회 확대 및 지역사회 관계망 형성을 지원하는 통합적 접근이 필요함을 시사한다.

title: Associations between hurricane stressors, social capital, and climate anxiety among individuals who experienced Hurricanes Helene and Milton
authors: Francis S. Dalisay; Wenlin Liu; Masahiro Yamamoto; Haoran Chu; Jay Hmielowski; Young‐Rock Hong
abstract: This study examined how hurricane stressors and three forms of social capital-bonding, bridging, and linking-are associated with climate anxiety, and whether the three forms of social capital would moderate the relationship between hurricane stressors and climate anxiety. We analyzed data from a cross-sectional survey (N = 1,342) administered in Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina following Hurricane Helene and in Florida following Hurricane Milton in 2024. Results showed that hurricane stressors were positively associated with climate anxiety, and these associations held after controlling for symptoms of generalized anxiety. Findings also revealed a nuanced role of social capital. Bonding social capital had a direct negative association with climate anxiety. However, our results suggested that bonding social capital's protective role is conditional and reverses under high stress. That is, bonding social capital weakened the relationship between hurricane stressors and climate anxiety only when hurricane stressors were low. As stressors accumulated, bonding social capital strengthened the association between stressors and climate anxiety. In contrast, both bridging and linking social capital were positively associated with climate anxiety and strengthened the positive relationship between hurricane stressors and climate anxiety. We discussed theoretical insights and practical implications.

title: Social Capital and the Well‑Being of Underprivileged Children and Youth in Hong Kong: Evidence from a High-Income but Unequal City
authors: Wan Sang Kan; Siyuan Guo; Jialiang Cui
abstract: Abstract Hong Kong’s high living costs, dense housing, and competitive schooling create daily stressors that may affect the physical and psychological well-being of underprivileged children and adolescents. Guided by capital theory, this study examined the independent and joint associations of economic, cultural, and social capital with multiple well-being outcomes. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 529 primary and secondary students recruited through an NGO serving low-income and migrant households in Hong Kong. Measures included physical well-being, psychological well-being, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, weekly pocket money, access to cultural items, parent relations, and peer support. Hierarchical multiple regression models were used to examine the relative and incremental associations of different forms of capital with each outcome. Social capital, particularly parent relations and peer support, accounted for the largest increment in explained variance across all four outcomes. In the fully adjusted models, stronger parent relations and peer support were associated with higher physical and psychological well-being and with fewer depressive and anxiety symptoms. Cultural capital remained positively associated with physical well-being, but its associations with psychological outcomes attenuated after social capital was added. Weekly pocket money retained small positive associations with physical and psychological well-being but was not independently associated with depressive or anxiety symptoms after adjustment. Among underprivileged children and adolescents in Hong Kong, bonding social capital was the most consistent correlate of well-being across outcomes. The findings suggest that supportive parent and peer relationships may be more strongly associated with well-being than modest differences in discretionary economic or cultural resources in this sample. Longitudinal research is needed to clarify temporal ordering and possible causal pathways.

title: Does online informal social capital enhance healthcare technology adoption among older adults? The mediating role of attitudes
authors: Xin Guan; Cherry Tin Yan Cheung; Kam Kong Lit; Xuhong Li; Ada W. T. Fung; Xue Bai
venue: Journal of Human Behavior in the Social Environment
abstract: Healthcare technology adoption is critical for older adults to enhance healthcare access and autonomy. Limited research has examined the effect of social capital on healthcare technology adoption among older adults. Adopting the technology acceptance model and social capital theory, this study investigated the effect of online informal social capital on the mediating role of positive and negative attitudes between perceived usefulness and healthcare technology adoption. Five hundred ninety-seven participants were recruited to complete a personal communication regarding healthcare technology adoption. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used, and the results showed that positive and negative attitudes were significant full mediators. This study has enriched the two theories and provided practical implications for the social work practice, the healthcare field, and healthcare technology developers to address online informal social capital and attitudes in developing healthcare technology for older adults.

title: Racial Differences in Social Capital Volunteer Activities: A Mixed-Methods Longitudinal Study of How Race and Place Influence Opportunities
authors: Ester Villalonga-Olives; Abdolvahab Khademi; Alisha A. Crump; Christopher M. Amissah; Inez Adams; Candace Hall
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: Volunteering is a key component of social capital associated with improved health outcomes. However, it remains unclear how volunteer patterns differ by race and education and whether standard measures adequately capture racial and contextual differences in how volunteering is understood and reported. This mixed-methods study examined racial and educational differences in volunteer activities over time and evaluated how individuals from different racial backgrounds define, engage in, and value volunteering. This study used a mixed-methods longitudinal design combining secondary analysis of the Midlife in the United States (MIDUS) study (1995–2016; n = 5921) with qualitative interviews (n = 47) in the United States. The quantitative outcome was the number of self-reported volunteer hours per month across four domains: healthcare, youth-related, political, and other organizations. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine differences by race, volunteer context, and time, adjusting for age, gender, and educational attainment. Qualitative interviews used MIDUS item probes and open-ended questions to examine participants’ interpretations of volunteer work, unpaid activities, and forms of engagement. Black participants reported significantly higher volunteer hours than White participants (β = 0.97, p = 0.007). Volunteering varied by context, with higher engagement in school and youth-related (β = 1.12, p < 0.001) and other organizational activities (β = 2.80, p < 0.001) and lower engagement in political contexts (β = −0.45, p < 0.001), relative to healthcare settings. Volunteering increased modestly over time (Wave 2: β = 0.45, p < 0.001; Wave 3: β = 0.39, p < 0.001). Interaction analyses indicated that racial differences varied across contexts, with a significantly smaller increase in volunteering within “other” organizations among Black participants relative to White participants (β = −1.29, p = 0.006). Qualitative findings indicated that Black participants more often engaged in community-based and informal activities, including work within community organizations, whereas White participants more frequently participated in formal volunteering. Urban residents reported more flexible engagement compared with suburban residents’ structured participation. Volunteering is shaped by structural and contextual factors. Public health research and interventions should adopt more inclusive measures to better capture diverse forms of civic engagement.

title: The Paradox of Prudence: A Longitudinal Study of Strategic Cost Management, Social Capital Preservation, and Organizational Resilience in Prolonged Economic Contractions
authors: Rawat Rashmi; Prakash Vaishali; Kiran Navdeep; Dhanda Rajan
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper examines the concept of how companies can successfully survive extended economic downturns using strategic cost management and retain social capital and resilience. It looks at the conflict between cost reduction by aggression and preservation of relational assets, in the form of the so-called Paradox of Prudence. The study is based on a six-year longitudinal panel data of 214 firms in both manufacturing and service industries, in which the dynamic interrelations among cost intensity, social capital, and resilience outcomes are examined. The results suggest that aggressive cost reduction has a significant impact on enhancing the financial efficiency (0.42, p < 0.01) in the short term but also reduces social capital (0.37, p < 0.01). There is a strong positive relationship between social capital and organizational resilience (: 0.48, p < 0.01), and the association between cost strategy and resilience partially goes through social capital. Balanced cost strategies of firms have better long-term performance with recovery rates 23 points higher in the long term. The findings demonstrate the need to reconcile financial discipline with relational sustainability in the effort to achieve long-term resilience of the organization

title: Organisational mechanisms of the sharing economy: how platform and social capital integration enhances collaborative capabilities in SMEs supply chains
authors: Thammasak Kuaites; Kwanruthai Dechtongkam; Theeraphon Thueanphae
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how organisational mechanisms of the sharing economy, driven by digital platforms and social capital, contribute to enhancing the collaborative capabilities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) within the supply chains of emerging economies. It develops an integrated conceptual framework that links platform theory (PT) with social capital theory (SCT) and examines a structural model of key factors, including value chain (VC), information management (IM), market orientation (MO) and relationship management (RM). Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods research approach was used, using qualitative data from expert interviews to develop the model. This model was then tested using questionnaire data collected from 1,600 Thai SMEs, analysed through covariance-based structural equation modelling. Findings The analysis results indicate that VC integration, IM and MO significantly influence RM and enhance the collaborative capabilities of SMEs. The findings further demonstrate that VC integration functions as a strategic organisational mechanism that coordinates information, market responsiveness and relational governance. Crucially, the qualitative insights reveal that in environments characterised by institutional voids, social capital serves as a functional substitute for formal governance, “activating” digital platform mechanisms to alleviate resource constraints. The integrated PT–SCT model effectively explains how relational trust and structural platforms jointly configure collaborative behaviour among SMEs in the digital economy. Originality/value This research provides a novel, empirically validated model that demonstrates the generative integration of PT and SCT. It offers a unique perspective on how social capital serves as a functional substitute for institutional trust within SMEs supply chains in emerging economies. The findings fill significant theoretical gaps regarding the boundary conditions of PT in developing contexts like Thailand.

title: The Role of Social Capital in Explaining the Academic Performance of Bachelor Degree Students of the Faculty of Social Sciences at Kabul Education University
authors: Said Abdul Samad Moshtaq; Mohammad Jabar Sabir; Abdulhadi Haqani
venue: Journal of Social Sciences - Kabul University
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the role of social capital in explaining the academic performance of undergraduate students in the Department of Social Sciences at Kabul Education University. In terms of its purpose, this study was descriptive–analytical. Based on the nature of the data, it employed a quantitative research approach. Data were collected using a survey method, and the study was applied. The researchers collected data through two researcher-developed questionnaires. The first questionnaire measured social capital and included three dimensions and 21 items. The second questionnaire assessed academic performance and likewise comprised three dimensions with 21 items. The study population consisted of 360 undergraduate students enrolled in the Department of Social Sciences at Kabul Education University. Using Cochran's formula, the researchers determined a sample size of 186 participants. Participants were selected using a probability sampling technique with simple random sampling. The findings revealed a positive and statistically significant relationship between social capital and academic performance. Furthermore, the regression analysis indicated that social participation was the strongest predictor of academic performance, followed by social cohesion. In contrast, social trust did not demonstrate a statistically significant effect after controlling for the other variables. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening social capital to enhance students' academic performance.

title: Associations between the number of benzodiazepine receptor agonists prescriptions and social determinants of health, including social capital: an ecological study
authors: Sota Zukeran; Takuya Aoki; Yoshifumi Sugiyama; Masato Matsushima
abstract: BACKGROUND: The widespread prescribing of benzodiazepine receptor agonists (BZRA) is a public health problem worldwide. However, few studies have explored the relationship between the number of BZRA prescriptions and social determinants of health (SDH). Furthermore, to our knowledge, no reports have investigated the relationship between BZRA prescribing and social capital. Therefore, our objective was to conduct a prefecture-level ecological study focused on the number of BZRA prescriptions and SDH, including social capital. METHODS: We drew data for the number of BZRA prescriptions for April 2018 to March 2019 from The National Database of Health Insurance Claims and Specific Health Checkups of Japan Open Data. For the SDH, we obtained data on the relative poverty rate, Gini coefficient, unemployment rate, post-high school education advancement rate, number of single-parent households per 1,000 households, single-person household rate, and social capital scores from publicly available internet sources and previous report. We calculated the standardized claim ratio (SCR) for the number of BZRA prescriptions by prefecture. We then investigated the relationship between the SCR for BZRA and SDH through an ecological study using Spearman's rank correlation coefficients and multivariate regression analysis. RESULTS: The relative poverty rate, Gini coefficient, unemployment rate, number of single-parent households per 1,000 households, and single-person household rate were positively and significantly correlated with the SCR for BZRA. In addition, the social participation domain of social capital was significantly negatively correlated with the SCR for BZRA. In the multivariate analysis, the relative poverty rate and single-person household rate remained independently associated with higher BZRA utilization. However, the association between social participation and BZRA use was no longer significant after adjusting for these socioeconomic factors. CONCLUSIONS: This ecological study suggests that regional BZRA prescribing is associated with socioeconomic deprivation and household instability. While further individual-level research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms, our findings highlight the importance of addressing social determinants to manage regional disparities in BZRA use.

title: A social capital perspective on the complex determinants of satisfaction among residents in eldercare institutions: an empirical analysis from northern Xinjiang
authors: PAN Xinyu; Danyang Li; Yuxin Shi; Ke Ni; Yuanlin Li; Baifa Zu
abstract: Amid rapid aging, quality of life in eldercare institutions is a pressing concern. Although social capital is a key correlate of satisfaction, evidence on its bridging and bonding dimensions remains limited. This study examined the associations between these two types of social capital and satisfaction to inform efforts to improve institutional eldercare services. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in northern Xinjiang, China, between August 2024 and August 2025. Data concerning satisfaction with institutional eldercare services, sociodemographic characteristics, and participants’ social capital were collected. Hierarchical linear regression, quantile regression, and path analysis were applied to systematically investigate the associations between social capital and institutional care satisfaction, covering overall correlational patterns, quantile-specific distributions, and direct as well as indirect associative pathways. In total, 437 participants were enrolled, with a mean age of 83.6 years. The average satisfaction score was 3.790 ± 0.976. Hierarchical regression analyses showed that sense of belonging ( β = 0.223) and family affection ( β = 0.384) were positively associated with satisfaction with institutional eldercare services. Quantile regression further revealed that these associations were concentrated at the median satisfaction level ( P 50 ). At P 50 , family affection ( β = 1.292, p = 0.021), sense of belonging ( β = 0.466, p = 0.019), and number of offspring ( β = 0.353, p = 0.011) presented positive associations, whereas family support ( β =-1.214, p = 0.036) showed a negative association. Neighborhood atmosphere ( β = 0.296, p = 0.004) and monthly income ( β =-0.199, p = 0.029) were significantly associated with satisfaction only at the P 90 quantile. Path analysis indicated that family affection had the largest total associative coefficient (0.585), followed by number of offspring (0.433), sense of belonging (0.326), and neighborhood atmosphere (0.255). In contrast, family support (-0.623) and monthly income (-0.243) exhibited negative total associative coefficients. Associations between social capital and satisfaction varied by satisfaction level and support type. Sense of belonging and family affection were positively associated at the median level; neighborhood atmosphere was positively associated only among high-satisfaction residents; and family support was negatively associated among middle-satisfaction residents. Strengthening family affection and sense of belonging may improve care evaluations and help reorient family support from substitutive care toward emotional companionship, offering an entry point for improving institutional eldercare delivery.

title: The Impact of Social Participation Activities on Social Capital among the Hearing Impaired : The Mediating Effect of Digital Use Self-Efficacy
authors: Dong-Jin Park
venue: Journal of the Korea Academia-Industrial cooperation Society
abstract: 본 연구는 청각장애인의 온라인 사회참여 활동이 사회적 자본에 미치는 영향과 이들 관계에서의 디지털 이용효능감의 매개효과를 살펴보고자 하였다. 이를 위해 「2023 디지털 정보격차 실태조사」에 참여한 장애인들 중에서 자신이 청각장애인이라고 응답한 198명의 데이터를 추출하여 분석하였다. 연구 결과, 온라인 사회참여 활동은 사회적 자본에 직접적인 영향을 미치지 않았으나, 디지털 이용효능감을 통해 간접적으로 사회적 자본에 유의미한 영향을 미치는 것으로나타났다. 이는 온라인 사회참여 활동이 단독으로는 사회적 자본 형성에 제한적일 수 있으며, 디지털 환경에서의 이용효능감이 형성과 유지의 핵심 요인으로 작용함을 시사한다. 본 연구는 청각장애인에 대한 디지털 포용 논의에 있어 심리적 자원의 중요성을 강조함으로써, 기존의 물리적 접근 중심 정책의 한계를 보완하는 이론적 토대를 제시하였다. 또한 청각장애인을 위한 맞춤형 디지털 역량 강화 교육 등의 실천전략 개발이 필요함을 제언하였다. 한편, 본 연구의 한계를 지적하고, 향후 후속연구의 필요성을 제시하였다. 본 연구는 청각장애인의 온라인 사회참여와 사회통합을 위한 정책적 방향성과 실천적 시사점을 제공한다는 점에서 정책적·실천적 의의를 지닌다.

title: Can a Serving Leader instigate a Global Mindset? Social Capital as an intervening mechanism between Servant Leadership and Global Mindset
authors: Shadab Qazi; Fauzia Syed; Yasra Khalid; Fatima Shamim
venue: Journal of Innovative Research in Management Sciences
abstract: Purpose—Drawing from the social learning theory, this study examines the impact of servant leadership on global mindset, further, this study also investigates the mediating role of social capital between the relationship of servant leadership and global mindset. Study Design/methodology/approach—Using a cross-sectional data collection methodology, this study collected data from 370 individuals working in different multinational organizations. The data was analyzed using SPSS, AMOS and Smart-PLS through different statistical techniques, i.e., CFA, and PROCESS-macro. Findings—The results of this study illustrate that servant leadership has a positive impact directly on social capital and global mindset. Further, social capital, in turn, was found to have a positive influence on the global mindset of the employees. Additionally, social capital mediates the relationship between servant leadership and global mindset. Practical Implications—Initiatives should be taken for the development of policies that aim at incorporation of serving style of leadership in the top-level management. Measures should be taken to create an environment and culture that is more conducive to the building of social capital and global mindset of employees, especially working in the MNCs. Originality/Value—The present study was conducted with individuals of multinational organizations, with a focus on the global mindset of the employees. Further, this study contribution to leadership and organizational behavior domain explaining the impact of social capital and servant leadership to boost capabilities of the individuals working in multinational organizations to deal the challenges of globalization.

title: CSR AS A CATALYST FOR MSME PERFORMANCE: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF ENTREPRENEURIAL BEHAVIOR, SOCIAL CAPITAL, AND EMPOWERMENT IN PT BIO FARMA'S PROGRAM
authors: Rahmad Handoyo, Darsono Darsono, Drajat Tri Kartono, and Suminah Suminah
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR), with the aim of exploring how CSR programs, social capital, and empowerment influence small business behavior and performance. The methodology adopted for this research comprises a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative and qualitative. Data collection was carried out through a descriptive, explanatory survey to explore relationships between variables, while the qualitative aspect involves Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) to deepen understanding and validate finding]. The results obtained revealed the critical role of CSR partnerships, social capital, and empowerment in enhancing entrepreneurial behavior and small business performance. In the discussion section, these results are contextualized considering the theoretical framework, highlighting the implications and relationships identified. Possible discrepancies and limitations of the study are also considered in this section. The practical and theoretical implications of this research are discussed, providing insights into how the results can be applied or influence practices in the field of CSR. These implications could encompass policymakers and CSR practitioners, suggesting that CSR programs should focus on building social capital, empowering small businesses, and fostering entrepreneurial behavior to achieve sustainable business growth. This study contributes to the literature by practical contributions. The relevance and value of this research are evidenced by the importance of unrestricted funding, trust-based relationships, and self-reliance initiatives in fostering entrepreneurial behavior and improving small business performance.

title: The Effects of Social Capital on Life Satisfaction: Mediating Roles of Government Trust and Household Economic Perception, and the Moderating Effect of Region
authors: Yena Choi
venue: The Korean Journal of Local Government Studies
abstract: 본 연구는 사회적 자본(결속형･교량형･연계형)이 정부신뢰와 가구경제 인식을 매개하여 삶의 만족도에 영향을 미치는 구조가 거주지역(수도권･비수도권)에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지를 분석하고자 한다. 이들의 관계를 조절된 병렬 매개모형을 통해 검증하였으며, 분석 결과 결속형 자본은 삶의 만족도에 정(+)의 직접효과를 나타낸 반면, 교량형･연계형 자본은 지역유형에 상관없이 매개요인을 통해 간접적으로 삶의 만족도에 영향을 미쳤다. 그리고 사회적 자본의 간접효과에서는 경제적 간접효과가 제도적 간접효과보다 크게 나타났으며, 전반적으로 비수도권보다 수도권에서 간접효과가 더 증폭되는 경향을 보였다. 이러한 결과를 통해 향후 삶의 만족도를 높이기 위해서는 공동체 기반 정책을 추진하고, 온라인 정책 제안 플랫폼을 구축하며, 시민참여 채널의 실효성을 강화할 필요가 있다. 그리고 사회적 자본 정책과 함께 지역 유형에 맞는 경제적 기반 강화 정책이 병행되어야 할 것이다.

title: The Effect of Social Capital on Life Satisfaction Among the Elderly : Focusing on the Mediating Effects of Digital Activity Competence and Digital Efficacy
authors: 남서울대학교 사회복지학과 교수; So-Yun Choi
venue: The Journal of Next-generation Convergence Technology Association
abstract: 본 연구는 디지털 격차의 위험군에 속한 65세 이상 노인을 대상으로 사회적 자본, 디지털 활동역량, 디지털 효능감이 노인의 삶의 만족에 미치는 직간접 영향을 확인하였다. 2025년 디지털정보격차 실태조사 자료를 활용하여 1,280명의 자료를 분석하였다. 성별, 연령(75세 이하와 이상), 가구 유형(1인과 다인)에 따른 평균값을 비교한 결과 남성, 75세 이하, 다인 가구의 디지털 활동역량과 디지털 효능감 및 삶의 만족이 높은 것으로 나타났다. 사회적 자본과 삶의 만족에 있어 디지털 활동역량과 디지털 효능감의 다중매개효과를 구조방정모형으로 확인한 결과, 사회적 자본이 삶의 만족에 미치는 직접 영향은 β=.191(p=.013)이었고 사회적 자본→디지털 활동역량/디지털 효능감→삶의 만족의 간접효과는 p<.05에서 각각 β=.027과 .096으로 디지털 효능감의 매개효과가 디지털 활동역량보다 큰 것으로 나타났으며, 총효과는 β=.314(p=.021)로 확인되었다. 연구결과 노인의 디지털 정보격차 해소를 위한 사회적 자본 확충의 필요성과 관련된 방향을 제언하였다.

title: Efficacy of Training and Development on Employee Organizational Relationship and Social Capital Building in Nigeria Custom Service, Kwara State Chapter
authors: Ibraheem Shola Adegbemile; Adegbemile Maryam Lilian
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of Training and Development (T&D) programs in enhancing Employee Organizational Relationship (EOR) and building Social Capital within the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Kwara State Chapter. Against a backdrop of public sector demands for efficiency and reform, the research addresses the gap between T&D investments and their socio-relational outcomes. Utilizing a survey research design, data was collected from a sample of 278 officers using a structured questionnaire. Regression analysis was employed to test the hypothesized relationships. The findings reveal a significant positive effect of T&D on both EOR (R² = 0.479, p < 0.001) and Social Capital building (R² = 0.345, p < 0.001). This indicates that structured T&D initiatives substantially improve trust, commitment, and perceived organizational support while simultaneously strengthening interpersonal networks, inter-departmental collaboration, and shared professional identity. The study concludes that T&D transcends mere skill acquisition, serving as a critical strategic tool for fostering organizational cohesion and collaborative efficacy. It recommends the adoption of a sustained, dual-outcome T&D policy, the design of integrative and cross-functional training programs, and the establishment of relational metrics to evaluate T&D impact, thereby enabling the NCS to cultivate a more effective and resilient workforce for enhanced service delivery.

title: Reconstructing the Category of “We” Through Attitudes Toward Immigrant Inclusion: The Roles of Social Capital, Emotional Distance, and Media Use
authors: Hyejin Kang; DaEun Kim
abstract: 오늘날 이민자에 대한 포용은 단순히 소수 집단에 대한 관용의 문제가 아닌, ‘우리’라는 정체성의 경계를 재구성하는 과정이다. 이에 본 연구는 한국 사회에서 ‘우리’의 경계가 어떻게 변화하는지를 탐구하기 위하여, 이민자 포용 태도의 결정요인을 사회적 자본, 감정적 거리, 미디어 이용 유형을 중심으로 분석하였다. 분석 결과, 사회적 자본으로서 교량형 사회참여는 포용 태도를 높였으나, 결속형은 유의하지 않거나 부정적 영향을 주었다. 또한 외국인에 대한 감정적 거리는 사회자본과 포용 태도 사이에서 부분 매개효과를 보여, 이질적 집단과의 접촉이 정서적 친밀감을 매개로 이민자에 대한 포용적 태도로 이어짐을 확인하였다. 미디어 이용유형 역시 조절효과를 보였는데, 전통매체 중심 이용자들은 상대적으로 결속형의 부정적 효과가 강화되는 반면 교량형의 긍정적 효과는 더욱 두드러졌다. 이러한 결과는 ‘우리’의 경계가 사회적 네트워크, 정서적 친밀감, 정보 환경의 상호작용에 따라 확장 또는 축소될 수 있음을 시사한다. 앞으로 포용적인 ‘우리’로 나아가기 위하여 교량형 사회자본의 촉진과 감정적 공감대 형성, 균형 잡힌 미디어 환경의 조성이 이루어져야 할 것이다.

title: Effects of Public Rental Housing Environment on Residential Satisfaction Across Social-Mix Types - The Mediating Role of Social Capital -
authors: Hyun Jeong
abstract: 본 연구는 공공임대주택 거주자의 주거환경이 주거만족에 미치는 구조적 관계에서 사회적 자본의 매개 역할에 주목하면서, 사회적 혼합 유형에 따라 어떻게 차별적으로 작동하는지 실증적으로 검토하였다. 이를 위해 ‘서울시 공공임대주택 입주자 패널조사 3차년도’ 자료를 활용하여 구조방정식모형의 분석을 수행하였다. 분석 결과, 첫째, 임대주택만 거주하는 독립형에서는 단지환경을 통한 사회적 자본의 매개 경로가 유의했으나, 혼합 단지에서는 근린환경을 경유하는 매개 경로가 유의하게 나타나 혼합 방식에 따른 차별성을 입증했다. 둘째, 단지환경은 모든 유형에서 주거만족에 정(+)의 영향을 미치는 요인이었으나, 혼합 수준이 향상될수록 주거만족도 결정 시 주택 및 근린환경까지 입체적으로 고려하는 양상이 확인되었다. 셋째, 사회적 혼합도가 가장 높은 동내 혼합형의 경우, 주민 간 형성된 사회적 자본이 주거만족에 강력한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤으나, 단순한 공간적 혼합이 사회적 자본의 형성으로 이어지는 데는 한계를 보였다. 이러한 분석 결과를 토대로, 독립형 단지 내부의 시설 지속적인 관리 및 질적 향상, 혼합 단지 주변의 광역적 근린 인프라 확충, 사회적 혼합 정책의 본질적 목표 달성을 위한 정성적 중심의 공동체 관리 체계 제도화 등의 정책 대안을 마련하는 것이 바람직할 것이다.

title: Optimal Allocation Model for Social Capital Resources in Community Health Management Based on Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: L. Jin
abstract: In community health management resource allocation, the difficulty in quantifying social capital and the inefficiency of multi-agent collaboration lead to imbalanced allocation. This problem, mirrored in the textile industry’s complex supply chain where poor coordination and unquantifiable supplier relationships cause imbalanced raw material and production allocation, is addressed by this paper. We propose a model integrating dynamic social network embedding with hierarchical multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL). A graph neural network extracts node embeddings from time-series interaction data to achieve a quantitative representation of social capital. A hierarchical multi-agent architecture is constructed using heterogeneous agents responsible for demand response and resource scheduling, respectively. A joint reward function integrates health improvement, resource utilization, and network fairness, while a counterfactual baseline mechanism allocates local credit to improve policy learning accuracy. Furthermore, a parameter-sharing MAPPO (Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization) algorithm with entropy regularization is employed under a centralized training and distributed execution framework to achieve stable collaborative decisionmaking. Beyond community governance, the proposed dynamic graph representation and multi-agent optimization strategy provides a computational framework for distributed information coordination and adaptive resource scheduling in intelligent electromagnetic sensing and communication environments, where reliable network interaction and efficient information propagation are critical. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an average Gini coefficient of 0.18–0.29 for normalized healthcare demand satisfaction and a social capital activation rate of 79.3%±3.6%, significantly improving allocation fairness and utilization efficiency. By quantifying social capital and enhancing multi-agent collaboration, this study provides an effective framework for alleviating distribution imbalance while offering methodological insights for intelligent resource management in complex networked engineering systems.

title: The Relationship Between Job Identity and Service quality of Nursing Care Workers: The Mediating Effect of Job Stress and Social Capital
authors: Hae-Hyoung Rhee; Hye-Sun Kim
abstract: Objectives This study examined the effect of care workers’ occupational identity on service quality and verified the mediating effects of job stress and social capital. Methods A survey was conducted from May to September 2025 with 600 care workers employed in nursing homes and home-visit care agencies in Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Incheon. The data were analyzed using a structural equation model to test the direct effect of occupational identity on service quality and the mediating effects of job stress and social capital. Results Occupational identity was found to enhance social capital and reduce job stress, as well as to enhance service quality. In the relationship between occupational identity and service quality, the mediating effect of social capital was significant, whereas the mediating effect of job stress was not significant. Conclusions Improving care workers’ treatment, developing training programs to strengthen occupational identity, and building networks and support systems to foster social capital are necessary. Policy and practical interventions based on these efforts are required.

title: Does social capital matter for subjective well-being in a least developed country context? Using a pseudo-panel approach
authors: Kelemu Fenta Gebeyehu; Yuying Tong; Migbaru Alamirew Workneh; Lei Jin
venue: Journal of Human Behavior in the Social Environment
abstract: While it has been argued that in the least developed societies, due to the weakness of formal institutions, social capital may be significantly linked with well-being, its effect has shown differential effects for individuals with different statuses. Despite this ambiguity, its well-being effects in the least-developed countries, such as Ethiopia, remain under-researched. Moreover, current cross-sectional studies often neglect the influence of various dimensions of social capital on well-being and face problems of endogeneity.To address this gap, we rigorously examine whether the multiple aspects of social capital matter for subjective well-being in Ethiopia. Method: Utilizing a sample of 9,229 individuals from eight waves of the World Gallup Poll survey data, we analyzed the effect of multiple aspects of social capital on subjective well-being. We employ a novel pseudo-panel approach to tackle endogeneity issues using a system-generalized method of moments estimator.Our analysis reveals that perceived support, friendship, and civic engagement significantly affect subjective well-being, exhibiting distinct and counterintuitive effects on life satisfaction and emotional well-being. Social support is a robust predictor of life satisfaction and both positive and negative emotional well-being.Our main findings revolve around the unique results that, though the multiple aspects of social capital positively contributed to subjective well-being, they are not always beneficial for well-being, where friendship opportunities and perceived support inversely affect life satisfaction and positive emotional well-being, respectively. Despite uncovering the positive and adverse effects of social capital on well-being, we recommend that future studies account for the collective dimensions of social capital and test the results with a larger sample size and by examining the mechanisms underlying these effects.By addressing the repeated research calls from the least developed world, the study contributes to the existing literature by strengthening the causal links between social capital and subjective well-being using a pseudo-panel approach that treats independent cross-sectional data as synthetic panels. This could aid policymakers and researchers in clarifying the ambiguity of the well-being effect of social capital while designing targeted interventions to enhance well-being in the least developed countries.

title: A Study on the Effects of Social Capital on Resident Participation Intention in Self-Governance: Focusing on the Mediating Effects of the Theory of Planned Behavior
authors: Jung Ah Choi; Yongchan Song
abstract: 본 연구는 사회자본이 주민자치 참여의도에 미치는 영향 경로에서 계획된 행동이론(TPB)의 매개효과를 실증적으로 규명하는 것을 목적으로 서울특별시, 광역시 2곳, 도 2곳에서 총 600명을 대상으로 설문조사를 실시하고, 위계적 회귀분석과 부트스트랩 매개효과 검증을 수행하였다. 분석 결과, 사회자본만 투입 시 교량형 사회자본이 참여의도의 핵심 예측 요인이었으며, 계획된 행동이론 요인을 추가하면 설명력이 상당히 상승하고 지각된 행동통제가 가장 강한 영향력을 보였다. 매개효과 분석에서 결속형 사회자본은 태도·주관적 규범·지각된 행동통제를 통해 거의 완전매개 구조를 보인 반면, 교량형 사회자본은 직접·간접 경로가 공존하는 부분매개 구조를 나타내어 사회자본 구성요소별 차별적 작동 방식이 확인되었다. 또한 성별에서는 참여에 대한 태도와 참여의도에서 남성이 유의하게 높았고, 연령대별로는 40대가 대부분 요인에서 가장 낮은 수준을 보였다. 이러한 결과는 주민자치 활성화를 위해 단순한 제도 정비를 넘어 주민의 행동통제감 강화, 사회적 연결망 확충, 참여 규범의 형성, 그리고 성별·세대별 맞춤형 접근이 필요함을 시사한다.

title: Developing a Sustainability Model for Community Enterprises in Eastern Thailand: An Integration of Sufficiency Economy Philosophy, Innovation Management, Social Capital
authors: Jantana Ridsomboon; Naris Uraipan; Atchawan Saraithong; Pawinee Thongyamd; Vicharinee Sawasdee; Sriwaree Sujaritchai
abstract: This study investigates the structural relationship and influence pathways among sufficiency economy philosophy, innovation management, social capital, and sustainability of community enterprises in Eastern Thailand. Using a stratified random sampling approach, data were collected through online questionnaires and emails from community enterprise representatives, resulting in 486 valid responses. Structural equation modeling (SEM), integrating confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and path analysis, was employed to examine the proposed relationships. The study reveals that the proposed structural model demonstrates a good fit with the empirical data. Sufficiency economy philosophy exerted significant direct effects on innovation management and social capital and also influenced sustainability both directly and indirectly through these mediating variables. The findings further demonstrate that innovation management and social capital play critical roles in enhancing the sustainability and governance capacity of community enterprises. Moreover, sufficiency economy philosophy, innovation management, and social capital jointly explained 63% of the variance in sustainability, indicating the model’s strong predictive power. From a policy and practical perspective, the results provide valuable guidance for policymakers and development agencies in designing community enterprise support programs that integrate sufficiency economy principles with innovation capacity building and social capital strengthening, thereby fostering sustainable regional development in Eastern Thailand.

title: Analysis of the Social Capital of Local Stakeholders' Network in the Context of Watershed Co-Management(Case Study: Khoda Afarin District)
authors: Golbarg Bakhshesh; Mehdi Ghorbani; Seyed Amirhossein Garakani; Fatemeh Jalili Alishah; Ahmad Naderi; Sajjad Amiri
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: 1. Introduction Watershed management is an integrated approach for protecting water and soil resources, improving ecosystems, and reducing environmental risks. Co-management, involving local stakeholders, is vital for addressing water scarcity and climate change. Trust among stakeholders is crucial for decision-making, and Social Network Analysis (SNA) helps assess collaboration. Economic, social, and land ownership factors influence participation. Khoda Afarin faces soil erosion and floods, requiring trust-based strategies, yet research gaps remain. This study analyzes trust networks to enhance watershed management. 2. Methodology Khoda Afrin District, located in the northeastern part of East Azerbaijan Province, borders the Republic of Azerbaijan, Armenia, and Ardabil Province. With a population of approximately 34,977 people, this region faces significant challenges, including widespread migration and a decline in job opportunities. The economy of the region is primarily dependent on agriculture and livestock farming. However, climate change and soil erosion have resulted in a decrease in productivity. Projects such as the Khoda Afrin Dam and the Aras Free Zone have had an impact on the development of the. The Aras River is the main source of water, but soil erosion and frequent floods pose serious threats. Integrated watershed management is essential to address these challenges and achieve sustainable development through co-management. The research method of this study is a mixed-methods approach, utilizing both survey and applied methods. Data were collected through a social network analysis questionnaire, face-to-face interviews, and direct observation. The statistical population consists of 40 members of the Rural Development and Progress Association in three villages: Sharfe, Bastamlou, and Dormoshkelano. The validity of the questionnaire was confirmed by expert opinions, and its reliability was verified with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 92%. To evaluate the components of social capital, a Likert scale was used. Social network analysis, using UCINET software, was employed to examine the relationships among stakeholders and design participatory management. Various network indices, such as density, centralization, and average geodesic distance, were analyzed to assess interactions and natural resource management. 3. Results The results of the study showed that in the selected villages, the highest population is in the age group under 40, with Bostamlou having the highest percentage of people under 40, and Sharfe having the highest percentage of people aged 50 to 60 and over 60. Regarding gender distribution, in all the villages, men outnumber women, and the greatest gender disparity was observed in the village of Sharfe. Additionally, Bastamlou has a more balanced gender distribution compared to the other villages. Regarding household structure, Bastamlou has the highest percentage of large households, while Dormoshkelano has the highest percentage of small households. In terms of social networks, Bastamlou has the highest trust network density, while Dormoshkelano has the highest collaborative network density. In examining the concentration of in-degree and out-degree in social networks, Bastamlou has the highest in-degree concentration in the collaborative network. In Dormoshkenlo, the highest out-degree concentration is in the trust network, and in Sharfe, the in-degree concentration in both trust and collaborative networks is evenly distributed. Finally, the reciprocity, transferability, and average geodesic distance indices also indicated differences in the trust and collaborative networks among the villages. 4. Discussion The findings of the research indicate that the structure of social networks among local stakeholders in the three studied villages impacts the success of participatory management. In the village of Bastamlou, with a younger population and larger households, there is greater social cohesion and trust, leading to higher participation. In contrast, in the village of Sharfe, with an older population and smaller households, the networks are weaker, and participation is lower (Persdzink et al., 2022). The analyses show that in Bastamlou, participation and trust are more evenly distributed, and the relationships are more stable, while in Sharfe and Dormoshkelano, the high concentration of certain individuals in the networks leads to reduced cooperation and cohesion (Ghobani et al., 2025). Additionally, the transitivity of ties in Bastamlou is higher, contributing to greater network stability and participation, while in Sharfe, this transitivity is lower. The findings also indicate that the reduction in geodesic distance in Bastamlou facilitates faster exchange of information and participation (Jiang et al., 2015; Ari et al., 2024). 5. Conclusion The results of the analysis of the social networks of local stakeholders in three villages of Khoda Afarin district show that the existence of dense networks and bidirectional, stable relationships are key prerequisites for effective participatory management in the watershed area. The village of Bastamlou, with greater social cohesion and more active participation, offers an appropriate model. To improve other villages, strengthening social capital and building trust among stakeholders is essential. It is recommended to identify central actors and hold educational workshops to create stronger social networks. Additionally, in villages with an older population, new social ties should be established. These findings align with the research of Jarrigo et al. (2024), which has shown that high social capital leads to increased trust and improved decision-making processes in natural resource management. Author Contributions In the preparation and writing of this article, all authors have contributed equally and jointly. All stages of the research, from study design and data collection to analysis of results and final writing of the article, are the result of collaboration and collective agreement of all authors. Data Availability Statement Data available on request from the authors. Acknowledgements We are very grateful to everyone who assisted us in conducting this research. Ethical Considerations All authors affirm that this research was conducted in accordance with ethical standards, with no data fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism. Funding This research was conducted with the support of the Natural Disasters Research Institute and the Social Business Institute of the University of Tehran. The authors would like to express their sincere gratitude and appreciation to these institutions for their valuable support. Conflict of Interest The authors declare no conflict of interest

title: The Effects of Self-Efficacy and Self-Understanding on Career Decisiveness among Educationally Marginalized Youth: The Mediating Role of Social Capital
authors: Ju Yeon Kim; Jaei Kim; Youngsil Cho
abstract: 본 연구는 교육소외 청소년의 자기효능감과 자기이해가 진로결정성에 미치는 영향과 사회적 자본(주변·성인·친구)의 하위요인별 매개효과를 검증하는 데 목적이 있다. 2024년 삼성꿈장학재단 배움터 교육지원사업 참여 교육소외 청소년 1,090명을 대상으로 SPSS 26.0과 PROCESS Macro를 활용하여 회귀분석 및 부트스트래핑을 실시하였다. 분석 결과, 첫째, 교육소외 청소년의 진로결정성은 전반적으로 낮은 수준이었다. 둘째, 자기효능감은 진로결정성에 직접적 영향을 미치지 않았으나, 사회적 자본(성인)을 통해 정적 간접효과를 보였다. 셋째, 자기이해는 진로결정성에 직접적인 정적 영향을 미쳤으며, 사회적 자본(성인)을 통한 부적 간접효과를 나타냈다. 이러한 결과는 교육소외 청소년의 진로결정성 향상을 위해 개인 내적 자원 강화와 함께 성인과의 지지적 관계 형성이 중요함을 시사한다. 본 연구는 교육소외 청소년의 개인적·사회적 요인과 사회적 자본을 통합적으로 분석함으로써 향후 교육복지정책 및 진로교육 실천에 기초자료를 제공한다는 데 의의가 있다.

title: “It's how you say it”: Text-based measures of social capital and how it shapes public evaluations of environmental risk perceptions
authors: Rotem Dvir; Hyunseok Hwang; Carol L. Goldsmith
venue: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
abstract: This study examines how different dimensions of social capital shape individuals’ perceptions of environmental health risks. While prior research primarily relies on survey-based measures capturing networks, trust, and participation, such approaches often overlook the affective and emotional aspects of social capital. We introduce an approach that leverages text-based measures to capture individuals’ emotional attachment to their communities.
