Using survey data collected in Texas (2023-24), we employ multiple text analysis tools (including the use of LLM) to demonstrate the validity of using textual data as an indicator of individual social capital. Then, we combine the new text-based score measure with traditional survey indices and estimate their relationship with perceived health risks from environmental hazards. Our results assessing specific health risks like respiratory disease and mental health conditions reveal contrasting effects: text-based social capital is positively associated with higher risk perceptions, whereas survey-based measures are negatively associated with perceived risks. These findings highlight the multidimensional nature of social capital and demonstrate the value of integrating diverse measurement approaches to better understand public responses to environmental hazards.

title: The Mediating Effect of Social Capital in the Relationship between Health Promotion Behavior and Quality of Life among Community-Dwelling Older Adults
authors: Jin Yoo
venue: The Korean Journal of Local Government Studies
abstract: 본 연구는 지역사회 노인의 건강증진행위가 삶의 질에 미치는 직접효과를 검증하고, 이들 관계에서 사회적 자본의 매개효과를 분석하는 데 목적이 있다. 이를 위해 부산광역시에 거주하는 만 60세 이상 노인 774명을 대상으로 설문조사를 실시하였으며, 수집된 자료는 SPSS 30.0과 AMOS 30.0을 활용하여 구조방정식모형으로 분석하였다. 건강증진행위는 신체건강행위, 일상생활관리, 정신건강행위로, 사회적 자본은 신뢰, 참여, 네트워크로, 삶의 질은 신체적 영역과 환경적 영역으로 세분화하였다. 분석 결과, 신체건강행위와 정신건강행위는 삶의 질의 신체적 영역과 환경적 영역에 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤으며, 일상생활관리는 신체적 영역에만 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤다. 사회적 자본의 하위요인 중 네트워크는 삶의 질의 두 영역에 모두 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤고, 신뢰는 신체적 영역에 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤다. 반면 참여는 환경적 영역에 부(-)의 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 매개효과 검증 결과, 네트워크는 건강증진행위와 삶의 질의 관계에서 주요한 매개변수임을 확인하였다. 특히 정신건강행위는 신뢰와 네트워크를 매개하여 삶의 질에 영향을 미치는 주요 건강증진행위 요인으로 나타났다. 본 연구는 건강증진행위, 사회적 자본, 삶의 질을 하위요인별로 세분화하여 지역사회 노인의 삶의 질 형성 경로를 구체적으로 검증하였다는 점에서 의의가 있다. 연구결과는 노인의 삶의 질 향상을 위해 신체적 건강관리 중심의 접근을 넘어 정신건강 증진과 사회적 관계망 강화를 통합한 지역사회 기반 건강증진 프로그램의 필요성을 실증적으로 뒷받침한다.

title: Does rural talent cultivation enhance farmers’ social capital? Evidence from the ‘One Village, One University Student’ project
authors: Jiawei Wang; Xia Kuang; Hui Yang; Wenmei Liao; Hailan Qiu
abstract: Using the One Village, One University Student (OVOUS) project as an example and drawing on survey data from 2,552 farmers in 12 counties (county-level cities/districts) in Jiangxi Province, China, this study employs an endogenous switching probit (ESP) model to empirically examine whether participation in rural revitalization talent-training programs enhances farmers' social capital. The results show that: (1) participation significantly increases farmers' bonding social capital by 6.8 percentage points (ATT = 0.068, SE = 0.002), suggesting that systematic education not only strengthens individual capabilities but also facilitates the expansion of social networks; (2) correspondence education yields a stronger social-capital-promoting effect than distance education, with estimated effects of 8.1 and 5.8 percentage points, respectively, highlighting the potential role of face-to-face interaction and repeated social engagement in enhancing farmers' bonding social capital; and (3) older farmers experience slightly larger gains in bonding social capital than younger farmers (10.8 versus 10.5 percentage points), and female farmers experience substantially larger gains than male farmers (12.8 versus 5.1 percentage points), indicating stronger marginal returns among groups with relatively weaker social networks. Overall, the findings reveal that rural talent policies generate important spillover value by fostering social capital accumulation. This implies that future policy design should jointly consider the dual effects on human capital and social capital and, in light of group heterogeneity, improve the matching mechanisms between training modalities and target participants to enhance policy precision and overall effectiveness.

title: Housing Policy Factors and Social Capital as Determinants of Homeownership among Middle-Income Earners in Libya: The Mediating Role of Housing Quality
authors: Salem Khalifa Salem Kasah; Gazi Md. Nurul Islam
venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
abstract: Homeownership remains a major challenge for middle-income households in Libya because of affordability constraints, limited institutional support, and continuing economic and political instability. This study examines the effects of Housing Policy Factors, Social Capital, and Housing Quality on Homeownership among middle-income earners in Tripoli, Libya. It also assesses the mediating role of Housing Quality in the relationships between the independent variables and Homeownership. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted using a structured questionnaire. Of the 300 questionnaires distributed, 240 were returned and 219 valid responses were retained for analysis using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that Housing Policy Factors have a significant positive direct effect on Homeownership and a significant indirect effect through Housing Quality. Social Capital does not significantly affect Homeownership directly, although it has a significant positive effect on Housing Quality. The direct relationship between Housing Quality and Homeownership is positive but not statistically significant, and the indirect effect of Social Capital on Homeownership through Housing Quality is also not significant. These findings indicate that institutional housing support is more directly associated with homeownership than community relationships alone. The study contributes evidence from Libya by integrating policy, social, and housing-quality dimensions within one analytical framework. It recommends coordinated policies that address affordability, institutional support, and the quality of housing available to middle-income households

title: The Effects of Types of Digital Social Capital on Life Satisfaction among Older Adults Living Alone: The Mediating Role of Social Participation
authors: A-Yeong Jeong; Jun-Su Kim
abstract: This study aims to examine the mediating role of social participation in the relationship between digital social capital (bonding and bridging) and life satisfaction among older adults living alone. To achieve this, data were drawn from the 2024 Digital Divide Survey conducted by the National Information Society Agency(NIA), and responses from 2,300 single-person elderly households were analyzed. Hierarchical regression analysis was performed using SPSS Statistics 26.0 and PROCESS Macro v4.2, and the mediating effect was tested through bootstrapping procedures. The main findings are as follows. First, both bonding and bridging forms of digital social capital were found to have a statistically significant positive effect on life satisfaction. Second, in the relationship between digital social capital and social participation, only bridging social capital showed a significant positive association, whereas bonding social capital did not yield a significant effect. Third, social participation was positively and significantly associated with life satisfaction. Fourth, the mediation analysis revealed that bridging social capital exerted a partial mediating effect on life satisfaction through social participation, while no mediating effect was identified for bonding social capital. Based on these findings, this study proposes policy and practice implications aimed at enhancing life satisfaction among older adults living alone, with particular emphasis on differentiated approaches reflecting the distinct characteristics of digital social capital types and on strategies to promote social participation.

title: Differential pathways linking social interaction and Loneliness among university students in the age of artificial intelligence: the mediating role of Social Capital
authors: Juqin Yin; Hengkui Zhuo; Siyan Zhou; Zhinian Li
abstract: Based on Social Capital theory, this study explores the mechanisms linking emerging forms of social interaction and individual Loneliness among university students in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), from the perspective of Social Capital accumulation within AI-mediated social environments. Using survey data collected from university students, a Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach was employed to analyze the relationships among key variables. Specifically, social interaction preferences (including behavioral preferences and image presentation preferences) and embodied social competence were treated as independent variables. Social Capital was modeled as a higher-order latent construct comprising Bonding, Bridging, and Linking Social Capital, which jointly mediated the associations between social interaction characteristics and Loneliness.; and Loneliness was specified as the dependent variable. The results reveal differentiated mediating mechanisms within the AI-driven social interaction system. Online social interaction preference exhibits a dual-path effect on Loneliness: it directly increases Loneliness, while also exerting an indirect mitigating effect through Social Capital; however, this indirect effect is notably weak, suggesting limited psychological compensation. In contrast, embodied social competence emerges as the strongest predictor of Social Capital and significantly reduces Loneliness through higher levels of Social Capital. Furthermore, different sources of Social Capital demonstrate distinct effects in the context of AI-mediated social environments. The pathway linking online social interaction preferences to Social Capital was comparatively weaker, whereas the pathway from Offline Social Competence to Social Capital was substantially stronger. These findings suggest that different pathways of Social Capital accumulation may be associated with varying levels of protection against Loneliness. Overall, this study identifies differentiated associations among social interaction characteristics, Social Capital, and Loneliness, extends the application of Social Capital theory in AI-enabled socio-technical contexts, and provides important implications for promoting university students' social development and mental wellbeing.

title: The Influence of Existential Spirituality on the Quality of Life among Older Adults in Specific Local Areas : Focusing on The Mediating effect of Social Capital
authors: Sum Lee; Jihun Na
abstract: 본 연구는 노년기 실존영성이 노인의 삶의 질에 미치는 영향과 이 과정에서 사회자본의 매개효과를 검증하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 D광역시와 경상북도 G시에 거주하는 노인 350명을 대상으로 자기기입식 설문조사를 실시하였으며, 불성실 응답을 제외한 286부를 최종 분석에 활용하였다. 실존영성은 영적 안녕 척도(EWBS), 삶의 질은 COOP Chart, 사회자본은 신뢰, 상호호혜, 사회참여, 소속감으로 구성된 척도로 측정하였다. 성별, 연령, 학력, 경제상태, 배우자 유무, 가구유형을 통제한 후 SPSS 25.0과 PROCESS Macro Model 4를 활용하여 부트스트래핑(5,000회)으로 매개효과를 검증하였다. 분석 결과, 실존영성과 사회자본 모두 삶의 질에 정(+)적으로 유의한 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 또한 실존영성이 사회자본을 매개로 삶의 질에 미치는 간접효과 또한 통계적으로 유의하였다. 이러한 결과는 노년기의 삶의 질 향상을 위해 내적 의미 자원 강화와 함께 신뢰·연대·참여를 촉진하는 사회적 관계망 지원 전략이 병행되어야 함을 시사한다.

title: The Effect of Social Capital on Local Entrepreneurial Intention among Regional Youth: Serial Mediation of Place Attachment and Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy
authors: Kangwoo Kim; Changone Kim
abstract: [연구목적] 본 연구는 지역 청년의 사회적 자본이 로컬창업 의도에 미치는 영향을 분석하고, 지역애착과 창업효능감의 매개효과를 검증하고자 하였다. 특히 로컬창업 맥락에서 사회적 자본이 어떠한 심리적 경로를 통해 창업의도로 이어지는지를 규명하고, 창업의도 형성 메커니즘을 통합적으로 제시하는 데 목적이 있다. [연구방법] 사회적 자본, 지역애착, 창업효능감, 로컬창업 의도 관련 선행연구를 검토하여 연구모형과 가설을 설정하였다. 충북 북부권 중소도시 청년 및 예비창업자 189명을 대상으로 설문조사를 실시하였으며, 신뢰도 및 타당성 분석을 수행하였다. 가설 검증은 회귀분석과 Hayes PROCESS Macro(Model 6)를 활용하여 매개 및 순차적 이중 매개효과를 분석하였다. [연구결과] 사회적 자본은 로컬창업 의도에 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤다. 또한 사회적 자본은 지역애착과 창업효능감을 각각 증가시켰으며, 두 변수 모두 로컬창업 의도에 정(+)의 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 나아가 사회적 자본은 두 변수를 매개로 간접효과를 보였으며, 지역애착을 거쳐 창업효능감으로 이어지는 순차적 이중 매개효과도 유의하게 확인되었다. [연구의 시사점] 본 연구는 로컬창업 의도를 관계 자원, 정서적 유대, 실행 자신감이 결합된 과정으로 설명함으로써 이론적 확장을 제시한다. 또한, 지역 청년 창업 활성화를 위해 사회적 자본 형성과 창업효능감 강화를 결합한 접근이 필요함을 시사한다. 더불어 대학 및 창업지원기관의 교육 프로그램에서 네트워크 형성과 실천 중심 학습의 중요성을 제안한다.

title: Workplace social capital and turnover intention in nursing home caregivers: the mediating role of occupational burnout and the moderating role of professional certification
authors: Qiujie Zhang; Zhaoxi Han; Qinghui Peng
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined correlational associations among workplace social capital, occupational burnout, professional certification, and turnover intention in a sample of 222 Chinese nursing home caregivers, grounded in Social Capital Theory and Conservation of Resources Theory. Covariate-adjusted correlational results indicated a negative concurrent linkage between workplace social capital and turnover intention, with occupational burnout exhibiting a statistical mediating pattern in this linkage (indirect association = -0.0917, 95% bias-corrected bootstrap CI [-0.1883, -0.0199]). Professional certification functioned as a significant first-stage moderator of this statistical indirect pathway (index of moderated mediation = 0.1527, 95% bias-corrected bootstrap CI [0.0151, 0.3180]). The statistical indirect association via occupational burnout reached significance only among uncertified caregivers, while the corresponding indirect linkage was non-significant for certified caregivers. Higher concurrent workplace social resources corresponded to weaker burnout and turnover intention to a stronger degree for caregivers lacking professional certification with limited personal human capital endowments. This study integrates Social Capital Theory and Conservation of Resources Theory to delineate differentiated correlational patterns across caregiver subgroups, and puts forward targeted retention strategies differentiated by certification background for long-term care facilities.

title: Social capital, institutional support, and forest tenure mortgage loan demand: evidence from a staged demand framework in southern China
authors: Liushan Fan; Xingwei Ye; Yuanzhu Wei; Wenlan Wang
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
abstract: Background Forest tenure mortgage loans (FTMLs) are designed to activate forest tenure rights as collateral in China’s collective forest regions. However, household demand for FTMLs remains uneven, and it remains unclear how general credit demand is converted into product-specific FTML demand. Objective Using a 2018 baseline household survey from Fujian and Jiangxi Provinces, this study examines the mechanisms associated with staged FTML demand rather than estimating the current prevalence of FTML demand. It asks why some households report general credit demand and why some of those households further report FTML demand. Methods The analysis uses survey data from 962 forest households. A staged empirical strategy is adopted, including a full-sample Probit model for general credit demand, a conditional Probit model for FTML demand among households with general credit demand, a multinomial logit model for demand-stage outcomes, full-sample FTML-demand robustness checks, alternative social-capital specifications, Heck-probit diagnostic checks, and additional robustness checks excluding forestry discount-loan support. Results Social capital is positively associated with general credit demand and with the likelihood of entering the FTML-demand category in full-sample demand-stage models. Conditional on having general credit demand, forestry science and technology services are more directly associated with FTML demand. Forestry discount-loan support is also positively associated with FTML demand, but this association is interpreted cautiously because the variable may partly reflect prior exposure to forestry finance. After excluding forestry discount-loan support, the main staged-demand interpretation remains broadly consistent. Forest tenure certification shows suggestive evidence, but regression-based inference is limited by sparse observations and complete prediction. Conclusion FTML demand is best understood as a staged perceived-threshold process. Social capital is mainly related to credit-demand entry, whereas the transition from general credit demand to FTML demand depends on whether households cross a product-specific adoption threshold shaped by tenure credibility, forestry service support, and institutional finance exposure. The findings highlight the need to connect rural financial information channels with usable tenure documentation, technical extension, and transparent forestry-finance services.

title: Opposing effects of strong coworker relationships in times of sickness: a dual path between bonding workplace social capital and presenteeism propensity
authors: Sara Ravnkilde Nielsen; Vera Winter; Signe Pihl‐Thingvad
abstract: Abstract Background Social relationships have been emphasized as important for understanding the tendency to work while ill (presenteeism). Nevertheless, evidence on the underlying mechanisms explaining how social relationships affect presenteeism remains scarce. This study investigates whether the effect of strong coworker relationships (bonding workplace social capital) on presenteeism is mediated by stress and work engagement, as posited by a dual-path model. Methods We employ a time-lagged research design using survey data from a large Danish municipality. The sample includes 1,914 employees nested within 300 organizational units. Structural equation modeling was used to test a dual-path mediation model. Results We find evidence of a dual pathway between bonding workplace social capital (WSC) and presenteeism. While bonding WSC decreases presenteeism through reduced stress, bonding WSC simultaneously increases presenteeism through higher work engagement. Conclusions This study sheds light on opposing effects of bonding WSC on presenteeism. These opposing pathways underscore the complexity of social dynamics at work and suggest that public managers should recognize both the protective and unintended effects of strong coworker relationships, ensuring that high work engagement does not inadvertently promote unhealthy attendance behavior.

title: From digital access to social connectedness: the digital divide, bonding social capital, and depressive symptoms among older adults in China
authors: Yan Wang; Luwen Zhang; Wenbin Wang
abstract: Introduction: As population aging and digital transformation continue simultaneously in China, the digital divide among older adults has become an increasingly important social issue. This study examines the associations between multiple dimensions of the digital divide and depressive symptoms among older adults, as well as the potential role of bonding social capital. Methods: Drawing on three waves of data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS, 2018-2022), this study employs two-way fixed effects models and mediation analyses to examine the relationships between digital access, digital usage, digital outcomes, and depressive symptoms among older adults. Robustness checks were further conducted using propensity score matching (PSM), sample restriction adjustments, and replacement of the dependent variable. Results: Internet access was significantly associated with lower levels of depressive symptoms among older adults (p < 0.05). Compared with non-Internet users, entertainment-oriented, instrument-oriented, and mixed Internet use were all significantly associated with lower depressive symptoms (all p < 0.05). Digital outcomes were also negatively associated with depressive symptoms (p < 0.01). Bonding social capital showed significant indirect pathways linking all dimensions of the digital divide and depressive symptoms, with mediating proportions ranging from 5.95% to 26.67%. Period heterogeneity analyses further indicated that the associations remained generally stable before and during the COVID-19 period, although mixed Internet use exhibited a significant structural difference across periods (p = 0.036). Discussion: The findings suggest that the digital divide is closely associated with the mental well-being of older adults, while bonding social capital constitutes an important social pathway linking digital engagement and psychological health. Policy efforts should move beyond technological access toward broader digital empowerment and the construction of a more inclusive digital society for aging populations.

title: Comparative-Quantitative Analysis of the Relationship between Social Capital and Economic Instability with Suicide Rates (Intra-Country Study, 2011-2012)
authors: Afshar Kabiri; Mortaza Mahmoodzadeh
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: Suicide, due to its prevalence across societies both traditional and modern has attracted considerable attention from researchers across multiple disciplines, including psychology and sociology. The primary aim of the present study is to examine and elucidate the interprovincial differences in suicide rates within Iran. This research adopts a macro-sociological perspective, critically reviewing existing literature and social order theories to analyze the phenomenon of suicide. Employing a comparative-quantitative approach, the study utilizes secondary data spanning 2011–2021, with provinces serving as the unit of analysis. Empirical findings indicate that the linear combination of the examined variables accounts for approximately 0.63 of the variance in provincial suicide rates. Among the predictors, changes in inflation rates (β = 0.327) and unemployment rates (β = 0.220) exerted the strongest positive and direct effects on suicide rates, whereas life satisfaction (β = -0.146) and future outlook (β = -0.028) exhibited negative associations. These results suggest that provinces with higher inflation and unemployment experienced elevated suicide rates, while higher levels of life satisfaction and positive future expectations were associated with lower rates of suicide. Accordingly, the findings imply that individuals with weak social support and diminished social cohesion are particularly vulnerable to rapid, disjointed, and severe economic changes, which may increase the likelihood of suicide. Extended Abstract Introduction Suicide as a social phenomenon, although rooted in individual action, is sociologically, especially in the Durkheimian tradition, a function of social realities (integration and regularity). In Iran, statistics from the Forensic Medicine Organization show that the number of successful suicides increased from 2,598 in 2011 to 5,085 in 2013, and the suicide rate increased from 3.5 to 6 per 100,000 people. Furthermore, the distribution of suicide frequency among provinces is not uniform: Ilam province with an average rate of 0.116 and Sistan and Baluchestan province with a rate of 0.018 are at the top and bottom of this spectrum. This intra-country heterogeneity shapes the main research question: What factors explain the difference in suicide rates among Iranian provinces? The present study answers this question with a macro-sociological approach, simultaneously emphasizing the two constructs of social disorganization (as weak social capital, social ties, and institutional support) and economic instability (as inflation, unemployment, and declining GDP). The theoretical framework of the study is based on five axes: (1) Durkheim's suicide theory (1897), emphasizing two social trends of integration and regularity that cause selfish suicide (caused by weak cohesion) and anomic suicide (caused by disorder and economic crisis), respectively. Durkheim explicitly showed that financial crises and worsening economic conditions, such as the Vienna crisis of 1873, are accompanied by a sudden increase in suicide. (2) The theory of social disorganization (Wilson and Herrnstein), which emphasizes the weakening of institutions such as the family, school, and local communities and the reduction of the effectiveness of informal controls. (3) Stress theory (Agnew), which considers stressful events and lack of social support as the cause of negative emotions and ultimately deviant behaviors. (4) Social bond theory (Hirsch) which emphasizes the role of attachment, commitment, involvement and belief in preventing deviance. (5) The concept of economic disorganization, which refers to crisis, recession, decline in GDP, chronic inflation and structural unemployment. The combination of these theories provides an explanatory model according to which the weakness of social capital (social disorganization) on the one hand and economic instability on the other hand interactively create the basis for an increase in suicide. The main hypothesis of the research: “The suicide rate is a function of social disorganization and economic instability”. Methodology The research is a comparative-quantitative within-country study with a cross-sectional design (10 years). The unit of analysis is the 31 provinces of Iran in the period 2011-2014 (except for some indicators that continued until 2013). The data collection method is secondary analysis of existing data from three main sources: Suicide: Statistics from the Iranian Forensic Medicine Organization (number of successful suicides and rate per 100,000 people). Social capital indicators (social disorganization): Data from the social capital survey including eight dimensions: perception of the institutional success of the system, perception of the desirability of society, assessment of the future, perception of the existence of justice and equality, public trust, lawlessness, social participation, and life satisfaction. Economic indicators (economic instability): Data from the Central Bank and the Statistical Center of Iran including GDP per capita, Gini coefficient, unemployment rate, inflation rate, and economic participation rate. Findings The suicide trend in the country has been on the rise during the years 2011-2023. The suicide rate has increased from 4.7 in 2011 to 8.8 in 2023 (an increase of about 87 percent). Suicide attempts have also increased from 112 to 195 per 100,000 people. The provinces of Ilam (0.116), Kermanshah (0.110), Kohgiluyeh and Boyer Ahmad and Lorestan (0.088) have the highest average suicide rates, and the provinces of Sistan and Baluchestan, South Khorasan, Yazd and Mazandaran have the lowest rates. The average social capital indicators in the country are low: the highest life satisfaction is in Bushehr and the lowest in Kurdistan.The multiple regression model (simultaneous entry of 14 independent variables) showed: the multiple correlation coefficient is R=0.796 and the coefficient of determination is R²=0.633. In other words, the linear combination of variables explains about 63% of the variance in suicide rates across provinces (the adjusted coefficient of determination is 0.312, which indicates that about 31% of the variance is explained by taking into account the number of variables. Among the 14 variables, only four variables had a significant effect: Changes in inflation rate and unemployment rate are positive and direct; with increasing inflation and unemployment, the suicide rate increases, and the variables of life satisfaction and assessment of the future have a significant negative and inverse relationship with the suicide rate, meaning that with increasing life satisfaction and positive assessment of the future, the suicide rate decreases. Conclusion The research findings clearly support Durkheim's theoretical framework and post-Durkheimian theories. Increased inflation and unemployment (economic instability) as indicators of economic disorder and anomie are associated with increased suicide. This finding is consistent with the research of Hassel et al. (2014) in Greece, Amiri (2021) and Frasquiello et al. (2016). On the other hand, decreased life satisfaction and negative evaluation of the future (which are reflections of weak social capital and social disorganization) are associated with increased suicide. It is noteworthy that many dimensions of social capital (public trust, social participation, lawlessness, etc.) did not show a significant effect in the regression analysis, which is in line with the findings of Salehabadi (1400) and somewhat different from the findings of Bahador (1400). This may be due to differences in indexing, time period or level of analysis.Suicide in Iran, especially in the western and southwestern provinces, is a multi-causal social problem that is formed at the intersection of social disorganization (weak supports, low life satisfaction, pessimism about the future) and economic instability (inflation and chronic unemployment). Therefore, any effective intervention in reducing suicide requires an integrated and context-based approach. Therefore, it is suggested that designing social policies based on strengthening social capital (local participatory programs, support groups) along with economic stabilization policies (inflation control and unemployment reduction) be put on the agenda as preventive strategies for suicide.

title: Developing Social Capital for College Teaching: Exploring Connections Between Faculty Teaching-Focused Personal Networks and Evidence-Based Teaching
authors: Changhee Lee; Ross J. Benbow
abstract: Evidence-based teaching is widely recognized as critical for student learning in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine (STEMM), yet whether and how faculty develop these instructional practices through their social ties remains less well understood. To illuminate these dynamics, this study applies a social capital lens to investigate the role of faculty teaching-focused social networks. Using mixed-methods social network analysis of survey data from 868 faculty and 83 in-depth interviews, we examine the connection between instructors’ personal networks and their use of evidence-based teaching approaches for fostering communication, teamwork, and self-directed learning skills. Quantitative findings suggest that the size, range, and strength of faculty teaching-focused personal networks correlate with their use of evidence-based instructional practices. Complementing these associations, our qualitative analysis details the specific relational mechanisms, objects, and instrumental and expressive returns that faculty perceive as influential. We conclude by discussing implications for institutional policies and faculty development approaches, with findings suggesting that cross-sector professional connections and strategic network cultivation are critical for advancing evidence-based teaching practices in STEMM fields.

title: Individual Resilience as Human Capital Stock: Neighborhood Social Capital, Environmental Perceptions, and Dynamic Pathways Across COVID-19 Phases
authors: Rui Sun; Yiming Wang
abstract: Abstract This study, grounded in the social ecological theories, investigates how the pathways linking neighborhood relationships, perceived environmental quality (PEQ), and individual resilience (IR) differed between the COVID-19 pandemic and the post-pandemic period. The empirical focus is on Chinese international students (CIS) in the UK, who experienced a unique form of “double exclusion” during the pandemic. Multi-phase data collection was conducted through questionnaire survey using a pre-then-post design ( n = 146). Specifically, exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted to validate the dimensions of resilience as a contextual and dynamic construct, followed by a higher-order mediation model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to explore relationships between main latent constructs both during the pandemic and its aftermath. EFA confirmed sample adequacy (KMO > 0.9, Bartlett’s test p < 0.001) and validated the identification of first-order latent constructs for IR. Findings from PLS-SEM analysis revealed that during the pandemic, both structural and functional dimensions of neighborhood relationship were associated with IR through distinct mediation effects of PEQ. In the post-pandemic period, however, the pattern of associations differed: the mediation effect of PEQ on the relationship between structural neighborhood ties and IR was no longer significant, while PEQ remained a full mediator in the relationship between functional dimensions of neighborhood relationship and IR. These findings highlight the dynamic nature of IR as a stock of human capital. Neighborhood-based social capital functions as the primary investment, while perceived environmental quality acts as the efficiency channel through which this investment is translated into resilience outcomes. This interpretation offers an account of how resilience protection and accumulation may differ between crisis and post-crisis contexts.

title: Multidimensional social capital and latent anxiety severity profiles among Chinese medical graduate students: A multicenter cross-sectional study
authors: Wen Zhu; Xin Zheng; Ziwei Wang; Niannian Li; Yue Fang; Zhongliang Bai
abstract: Mental health issues, such as anxiety, are highly prevalent among medical graduate students. However, the potential relationship between social capital and anxiety symptoms in medical graduate students has not yet been investigated. Therefore, data were collected in 2024 from a multicenter sample of 2,587 medical graduate students obtained through multistage stratified sampling across northern, central, and southern Anhui Province. Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the 20-item Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS-20). Social capital was evaluated across six dimensions: social participation, social support, social connection, trust, sense of belonging, and reciprocity. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify latent anxiety severity profiles. Multinomial logistic regression was used to examine associations between social capital dimensions and anxiety severity-profile membership. The prevalence of anxiety symptoms among participants was 30.5%. Three latent anxiety severity profiles were identified: low (50.6%), moderate (18.6%), and high (30.8%). Lower levels of social support, social connection, and trust were associated with greater odds of membership in the moderate- and high-anxiety severity profiles. A higher sense of belonging was associated with lower odds of membership in the high-anxiety profile, whereas higher social participation was associated with greater odds of membership in the high-anxiety profile. Compared with the moderate-anxiety profile, membership in the high-anxiety profile was also associated with higher social participation and lower trust. Cognitive social capital, particularly trust and supportive connections, was consistently associated with lower anxiety severity, whereas structural participation showed a context-dependent association. These findings suggest that the quality and context of social relationships may warrant as much attention as the quantity of participation.

title: The Influence of Social Capital on the Participation of Farmer Group Members in the Rice Barn Program in Pendem Village, Junrejo District, Batu City
authors: Fadhila Hasna; Ismu Rini Dwi Ari; Salma Fitri Nugroho; Aisyah Nabilatul Ula; Laiza Afi Nurrohma
abstract: This study examines the relationship between social capital and farmer group members' participation in the Rice Barn Program in Pendem Village, Junrejo District, Batu City, East Java, Indonesia, a community-based food security initiative encompassing irrigation management, agricultural extension, and post-harvest processing. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted from January to March 2025, involving 193 farmer group members selected through accidental sampling from a population of 386. Data were collected via structured questionnaires and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirmed that social capital was validly represented by three dimensions, trust, social norms, and social networks, after removing two low-loading network indicators, with all constructs meeting convergent validity (AVE > 0.50) and reliability (CR > 0.70) criteria. SEM results showed that social capital was positively and significantly associated with farmer participation (β = 0.456; t = 7.319; p < 0.001), explaining 69.2% of the variance in participation (R² = 0.692). Trust emerged as the strongest contributing dimension, followed by social networks and social norms. These findings indicate that stronger social capital, particularly trust-based relationships, enhances farmer participation in village-based agricultural development programs. This study contributes empirical and methodological insights into social capital's role in participatory rural food security, including clarification on interpreting path coefficients, R², and effect size (f²) in PLS-SEM analysis.

title: Prospecting the Roles and Changing Aspects of Indigenous Knowledge as Social Capital in Conflict Resolutions of South Wollo Zone: The Case of Tehuledere Woreda
authors: Alebachew Kebede
abstract: The main objective of this research is to prospect the roles and changing aspects of indigenous knowledge as social capital in conflict resolutions of south wollo zone: the case of tehuledere woreda. The research design and approach of this study is a cross sectional design with a mixed research approach, where Survey, and in-depth interview were the primary sources of required data. The quantitative data was collected from 189 household respondents in the selected three kebele districts, namely: Ketie, Weldelulo, and Gobeya by using semi structured survey questionnaire. On the other hand, the qualitative data was collected from in-depth interviews with seven local elders, religious leaders and influential community members, continuing until data is saturated. The findings of this research indicated that land disputes emerged as the predominant source of conflict (51.9%), followed by property related disputes (24.3%) and family related issues (23.8%). The study emphasizes the significant reliance on respected elders and religious leaders in conflict mediation, emphasizing practices such as Shimgilina as central to community cohesion. However, the research also reveals a trend among younger generations towards formal legal systems, posing challenges for the preservation of traditional conflict resolution methods. The research highlights the urgent need for documenting and codifying indigenous knowledge, which is essential for enhancing its relevance and effectiveness in contemporary conflict management. Thereby contributing to socio-economic development South Wollo Zone, Tehuledere wereda.

title: The Bonding Paradox: How Social Capital and Financial Inclusion Shape the Micro-Entrepreneurial Strategies and Sustainable Livelihoods of Women Street Vendors
authors: Tran Thi Minh Phuong; Nguyễn Văn Phương; Quang Dao Vu; Srann Socheat; Nguyen Thi Cam Nhung
abstract: Women agricultural vendors serve as crucial intermediaries in the rural-urban food supply chain, bridging the last-mile gap between peri-urban production and inner-city consumption in Vietnam. While they play an essential role in ensuring urban food security, their own livelihoods remain deeply precarious, caught between rural obligations, persistent income instability, and urban regulatory exclusion. This study investigates the "Dual-Layer" impacts of social capital and financial inclusion on the sustainable livelihoods of 296 women agricultural and food vendors in Hanoi, utilizing a Random Encounter Sampling technique to accurately capture this mobile and hidden population. Employing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), the analysis reveals a striking "Bonding Paradox": while strong rural kinship ties (bonding capital) provide a direct safety net for basic survival, they exert no significant influence on micro-entrepreneurial strategies due to information redundancy. In contrast, bridging ties with diverse urban customers, linking ties with local authorities, and access to formal financial inclusion function as dynamic growth engines. Together, these external assets significantly improve livelihood outcomes by empowering women to execute adaptive micro-entrepreneurial strategies, such as product diversification and spatial mobility. These findings suggest that securing the informal agricultural economy requires policies that move beyond traditional community-based support. Policymakers must focus instead on integrating migrant vendors into formal urban financial and institutional networks, leveraging digital agricultural inclusion, and providing specialized microfinance products to promote genuine livelihood mobility rather than merely stabilizing poverty.

title: Strengthening disaster resilience in coastal Bangladesh: The roles of disaster knowledge, government policy support, social capital, and community risk perception
authors: Md. Mokit-Ul Hafiz; Mahmuda Siddika Meem; Ishtiak Hasan; Purbita Chakma; Nusrat Ansary; Projesh Chandra Das
abstract: Coastal communities in Bangladesh face growing threats from climate-driven disasters, making local resilience vital for survival and recovery. Grounded in protection motivation theory and resilience theory, this study explores how disaster knowledge, government policy support, and social capital help coastal households withstand natural hazards. It also examines whether community preparedness connects these factors to resilience, and whether risk perception changes these relationships. Using a two-wave survey design to minimize reporting bias, data were gathered from coastal households and analyzed using structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The findings show that disaster knowledge, government support, and strong social ties directly improve community preparedness, which significantly boosts overall disaster resilience. Community preparedness acts as a key bridge linking all three factors to stronger resilience, whereas perceived risk alone does not alter this impact. Finally, IPMA identifies local preparedness as the single most effective action area for disaster management. These results show that combining practical knowledge, government aid, and community networks gives policymakers a clear, practical roadmap to protect vulnerable coastal regions.

title: The Role of Bonding Social Capital and Nature-Based Water Management in Enhancing Ecotourism Resilience: A Case Study of Loksado in the Meratus Mountains
authors: Ahmad
venue: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
abstract: This study investigates how bonding social capital and nature-based water management jointly enhance the resilience of Loksado ecotourism in the Meratus Mountains, South Kalimantan. The Amandit River Basin faces hydrological degradation, and the Dayak Loksado community’s indigenous social capital remains poorly integrated into formal water governance. We hypothesize that bonding capital directly and indirectly strengthens ecotourism resilience through its influence on nature-based solutions (NbS) for water management, with bridging capital acting as a partial mediator. A quantitative survey was conducted among 168 respondents across four villages in Loksado District. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Our results show that bonding capital positively and significantly predicts NbS-based water management (β=0.421, p<0.001), which in turn significantly predicts ecotourism resilience (β=0.387, p<0.001). Bridging capital partially mediates the relationship between bonding capital and resilience. The model explains 64.3% of the variance in ecotourism resilience (R^2=0.643), with all structural paths exhibiting large effect sizes (f^2>0.35). The total effect of bonding capital on resilience is 0.359, while the total effect of NbS-based water management is 0.554. Hence, NbS-based water management serves as a partial mediator. This research contributes empirical evidence that indigenous social cohesion and traditional ecological knowledge are foundational, not merely ancillary, to sustaining ecotourism in hydrologically sensitive tropical mountain regions. The findings underscore the necessity of integrating community-level social capital with nature-based water strategies to bolster ecotourism resilience against environmental threats.

title: Determinants of the Employment Quality Index (EQI) among Venezuelan migrants in Peru: social capital, cultural integration, discrimination, and gender inequalities
authors: Héctor Javier Bendezú Jiménez; Aníbal Erik Romero Bendezú; Giovanna Chuchón Ochoa
venue: Revista iberoamericana de estudios de desarrollo = Iberoamerican journal of development studies
abstract: This study examines the determinants of job quality among Venezuelan migrants in Peru, a country that has received one of the largest migration flows in the region in recent years. It utilizes the National Survey of the Venezuelan Population 2022 and estimates a beta regression model to analyze how factors related to human capital, cultural integration, community social networks, perceived discrimination, and gender are associated with a multidimensional index of job quality. The results show that the level of education attained in Venezuela, continuous education in the host country, and cultural integration are positively associated with higher job quality, while community social networks and discrimination present negative associations. Additionally, gender disparities in access to better-quality jobs are evident. The study contributes to the literature on labor migration in Latin America by providing empirical evidence on the factors associated with job quality for migrants, highlighting the importance of policies aimed at reducing structural barriers and strengthening human and social capital to facilitate labor integration.

title: Determinants of worker participation in basic occupational health services: The roles of social capital and motivation among informal tourism workers in Indonesia
authors: Helfi Agustin; Muhammad Akhyar; Sumardiyono Sumardiyono; Sri Kusumo Habsari
venue: International Journal of Occupational Safety and Health
abstract: Introduction: Informal tourism workers play a vital role in Indonesia’s tourism economy but often lack access to occupational health protections, making them vulnerable to workplace hazards. Basic Occupational Health Services (BOHS) provide a preventive and promotive health framework for underserved sectors; however, participation among informal workers remains limited and the determinants of readiness to engage in BOHS are still poorly understood. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 222 informal tourism workers in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Data were collected using validated questionnaires and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to examine the relationships among health promotion, social capital, motivation, and readiness to participate in BOHS. Results: Social capital exerted the strongest influence on health promotion (β = 0.667, p < 0.001) and significantly affected motivation (β = 0.273, p = 0.003) and readiness to participate (β = 0.234, p = 0.001). Health promotion significantly predicted motivation (β = 0.240, p = 0.004) and readiness (β = 0.360, p < 0.001). Motivation partially mediated the effects of both social capital and health promotion on readiness. The model demonstrated moderate to substantial explanatory power (R² readiness = 0.534) and good predictive relevance (Q² readiness = 0.283). Conclusion: Strengthening BOHS participation among informal tourism workers requires strategies that enhance community social capital and motivational engagement rather than relying solely on information dissemination. Participatory health promotion and community-based initiatives may improve readiness and sustainability of BOHS programmes in informal tourism settings.

title: The Relationship between Social Capital and Subjective Age among Older Adults in Rural Communities: The Mediating Effects of Depression and Cognitive Function
authors: Eunji Kang; Aran Kim; Young-kyoung Hahn; Sung Won Choi
abstract: 본 연구는 농촌 노인을 대상으로 사회적 자본과 주관적 연령의 관계를 살펴보고, 이 관계에서 우울과 인지기능의 병렬 매개효과를 검증하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 한국인의 사회적 삶, 건강한 노화 프로젝트(Korean Social Life, Health and Aging Project; KSHAP)의 5차 조사에 참여한 만 59세 이상 노인 492명의 자료를 분석하였다. 분석결과, 사회적 자본은 우울과 부적 관계, 인지기능과 정적 관계를 보였다. 우울은 주관적 연령과 유의한 정적 관계를 보였으나, 인지기능은 유의한 관계를 보이지 않았다. 병렬 매개효과를 검증한 결과, 우울을 통한 간접효과는 유의한 반면, 인지기능을 통한 간접효과는 유의하지 않았다. 또한 사회적 자본과 주관적 연령 간의 총 효과는 유의하였으나, 우울과 인지기능을 고려한 후의 직접효과는 유의하지 않았다. 이러한 결과를 바탕으로 농촌 노인의 주관적 연령과 관련된 사회적·심리적 요인에 대한 시사점과 후속 연구의 방향을 논의하였다.

title: Social Capital, Subjective Norm, Product Knowledge, Environmental Concern, and Perceived Behavioral Control on Purchase Intensity of Recycled Products in MSMEs
authors: Doli Muhammad Jafar Dalimunthe; Tengku Ezni Balqiah; Heri Pratikto; Rifelly Dewi Astuti; Arif Qaedi Hutagalung
venue: Journal Of Management Analytical and Solution (JoMAS)
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of social capital, subjective norms, product knowledge, environmental concern, and perceived behavioral control on purchase intensity of recycled products in MSMEs in Indonesia. A total of 530 respondents were selected from North Sumatra, West Java, and East Java using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Square (PLS)-based Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results show that environmental concern, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms have a significant effect on purchase intensity. Furthermore, subjective norms mediate the relationship between social capital and perceived behavioral control on purchase intensity. This study provides insights into consumer behavior toward environmentally friendly products and supports the development of sustainable MSMEs.

title: Sport Engagement and Social Capital in Sport Settings: The Predictive Roles of Cultural and Educational Commitment among Athletes in Mazandaran Province, Iran
authors: Moradali Moradali Yazdan Nejad; Ali Rahmani Firoozjah; Ali Asghar Abbasi Asfajir; Majedeh Gholipour
abstract: The present study aimed to examine the role of the dimensions of the sport engagement model in explaining the components of social capital, namely interpersonal trust and social participation, among athletes in Mazandaran Province, Iran. This study employed a descriptive-correlational design with a quantitative approach. The statistical population consisted of active athletes across the cities of Mazandaran Province. A total of 359 participants were selected through convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Sport Engagement Model Questionnaire, comprising cultural commitment and educational commitment, as well as the Social Capital Questionnaire. Data analysis was performed using Pearson’s correlation coefficient and simultaneous multiple regression analysis. The results showed that both dimensions of sport engagement were positively and significantly associated with interpersonal trust and social participation (p < 0.001). Cultural commitment showed a strong positive correlation with interpersonal trust (r = 0.805), while educational commitment was also significantly related to interpersonal trust (r = 0.408). In addition, cultural commitment (r = 0.482) and educational commitment (r = 0.237) were positively and significantly related to social participation (p < 0.001). Multiple regression analysis indicated that the dimensions of sport engagement jointly explained 65.1% of the variance in interpersonal trust and 23.4% of the variance in social participation. Cultural commitment was the strongest predictor of interpersonal trust, whereas both cultural and educational commitment made significant contributions to the prediction of social participation. Overall, the findings suggest that greater sport engagement, particularly through strengthening cultural and educational commitment, may contribute to the enhancement of social capital in sport settings.

title: From social glue to green gold: how organisational social capital transforms SDG adoption into competitive advantage in manufacturing SMEs
authors: Bashir Aboaba Mojeed-Sanni; Hakeem Adeniyi Ajonbadi; Olatunji David Adekoya; Chima Mordi; Festus Edobor
venue: Journal of Organizational Effectiveness People and Performance
abstract: Purpose Manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face mounting pressure to adopt sustainable development goals (SDGs), yet sustainability is often perceived as a cost burden threatening financial performance rather than a source of competitive advantage. This study challenges the assumed trade-off by investigating organisational social capital (OSC) as the mechanism through which SDG adoption translates into enhanced financial performance and productivity. Design/methodology/approach We employ a sequential mixed-methods design: a survey of 287 manufacturing SMEs across Qatar, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, analysed via structural equation modelling, complemented by 12 in-depth case studies involving 47 interviews. Findings Results demonstrate that SDG integration, focusing on responsible production (SDG 12), decent work (SDG 8) and innovation (SDG 9), significantly predicts both bonding (ß = 0.64) and bridging capital (ß = 0.59). Both social capital dimensions strongly predict financial performance and productivity, fully mediating SDG–performance relationships. Moderation analyses reveal these effects are significantly stronger for smaller firms and when conventional resource availability is lower, confirming social capital functions as a strategic substitute for scarce tangible resources. Qualitative findings revealed three themes: sustainability practices signal ethical intent, activating trust and reciprocity internally, whilst embedding firms within institutionalised networks that confer legitimacy and access to resources externally. Practical implications The study frames sustainability as a relational investment producing improved performance, particularly for resource-constrained SMEs. Managers should prioritise SDG-aligned practices as strategic mechanisms for building social capital that substitutes for scarce tangible resources. Social implications By demonstrating that sustainability and profitability are compatible rather than competing objectives, this research encourages broader SME participation in achieving global development goals, particularly in resource-constrained emerging economies where adoption of sustainability has been limited. Originality/value This study uniquely integrates previously isolated sustainability and social capital literatures, providing rigorous mixed-methods evidence from the under-researched GCC manufacturing context. It specifies OSC as the precise mediating mechanism and identifies boundary conditions (firm size, resource availability) where relational resources become strategically indispensable, transforming social glue into green gold.

title: SOCIAL CAPITAL AND COMMUNITY-DRIVEN INITIATIVES IN OPOBO TOWN, RIVERS STATE, NIGERIA: BONDING, BRIDGING AND LINKING INSTITUTIONS IN PROJECT SUSTAINABILITY
authors: Ogolo Maxwell Kelefini; Girigiri,, Barinem Wisdom
venue: Rivers State University Journal of Society
abstract: Community-driven development (CDD) is an important strategy for addressing infrastructure and service-delivery deficits in rural and riverine communities in Nigeria. However, project implementation does not always result in sustainable community benefits. This study examines the relationship between social capital and the sustainability of community-driven initiatives in Opobo Town, Rivers State, focusing on bonding, bridging and linking social capital. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was adopted. Quantitative data were collected from 220 household heads across the four Amas of Opobo Town, while qualitative data were obtained through 18 key-informant interviews and four focus group discussions. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression, while qualitative data were subjected to thematic analysis. Findings indicate a high level of bonding social capital, with 82% of respondents reporting strong reliance on their War Canoe Houses for mutual support. Bridging social capital was moderate, while linking social capital was comparatively weak. Bonding social capital significantly predicted local resource mobilisation (β = .64, p < .001), bridging social capital predicted diaspora support (β = .42, p < .01), while linking social capital had the strongest association with project completion and sustainability (β = .71, p < .001). The regression model explained 68% of the variance in project sustainability. Qualitative findings identified elite capture, limited participation of women and youth, weak institutional coordination, and inadequate maintenance as major barriers. The study concludes that internal cohesion alone is insufficient for sustainable development and proposes an Opobo Development Partnership Model integrating traditional institutions, CDCs, government agencies, youth, women and diaspora organisations.

title: Analysis of the Role of Entrepreneurship Learning and Social Capital in Influencing the Entrepreneurial Interest of State Vocational High School Students in Gowa Regency
authors: Angelina Manase; Agus Syam; Pahrul; Sudarmi; Muhammad Alfa Sikar
venue: APSKI International Conference on Association of Indonesian Entrepreneurship Study Programs
abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine the influence of entrepreneurship learning and social capital on the entrepreneurial interest of state vocational high school students in Gowa Regency, both partially and simultaneously. The problem underlying this study is the still low interest in entrepreneurship among vocational high school students, most of whom are still oriented towards being job seekers rather than job creators, even though they have participated in entrepreneurship learning in the school curriculum. This type of research is quantitative research with an associative approach. The population in this study were all 478 state vocational high school students in Gowa Regency. Sampling was carried out using the Slovin formula with a sample of 218 students selected through proportional random sampling techniques. Data analysis was carried out using multiple linear regression analysis with the help of SPSS software. The results obtained: (1) Entrepreneurship learning has a positive and significant effect on the entrepreneurial interest of state vocational high school students in Gowa Regency partially; (2) Social capital has a positive and significant effect on the entrepreneurial interest of state vocational high school students in Gowa Regency partially; (3) Entrepreneurship learning and social capital simultaneously have a positive and significant effect on the entrepreneurial interest of state vocational high school students in Gowa Regency. These findings imply that efforts to improve the quality of effective entrepreneurship learning and strengthen students' social capital in the school environment are important factors in growing and developing sustainable entrepreneurial interest.

title: Implementation Of The Cooperative Performance Resilience Model Through Servant Leadership, Organizational Culture,And Social Capital At The Bintang 88 Muda Cooperative
authors: Adriana Madya Marampa; Helba Rundupadang
venue: EKOMBIS REVIEW Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi dan Bisnis
abstract: The type of research used in this study is quantitative research. The sample in this study was 40 employees at the Bintang 88 cooperative. The scale used in this study was an ordinal scale. The data collection technique used in this study was purposive random sampling. The data analysis technique used in this study was SEM PLS. The results of this study indicate that there is a relationship between social capital and the resilience of cooperative performance, social capital influences the resilience of cooperative performance, servant leadership influences the resilience of cooperative performance.

title: Bridging and Bonding Social Capital of Immigrant Mothers and Their Children’s Academic Achievement in Urban and Rural Areas: The Moderating Role of Private Education
authors: 선주 이; Meejung Chin
abstract: This study examined the relationship between immigrant mothers’ social capital and their children’s academic achievement, focusing on the moderating role of private education across urban and rural contexts. Social capital was categorized as either bridging (support from Korean networks) or bonding (support from co-national networks). We analyzed data from the National Survey of Multicultural Families on adolescents aged 13–18 years and their immigrant mothers. Multilevel modeling was employed to examine the association between immigrant mothers’ social capital and children’s academic achievement and to test the moderating effect of private education across the rural and urban samples. The results indicated that, in rural areas, immigrant mothers’ bridging social capital was positively associated with their children’s academic achievement, whereas their bonding social capital was not. In urban areas, neither social capital type was significantly related to academic achievement. Private education moderated the relationship between bridging social capital and academic achievement in only rural areas, with a positive association observed among children who did not participate in private education. These findings suggest that in rural areas, bridging social capital such as Korean networks is essential to provide more educational information and support for immigrant mothers, leading to improvement in their children’s academic achievement. Therefore, expanding opportunities for immigrant mothers to build ties with Korean parents and community members as well as obtain more educational resources will contribute to children’s educational outcomes.

title: Strategic Approaches to Enhancing Financial Performance: Financial Literacy and Social Capital as Pillars of Business Resilience Amid Global Economic Challenges
authors: Yuliusman Yuliusman; Wirmie Eka Putra; Fredy Olimsar; Nyimas Dian Maisyarah; Dahmiri Dahmiri
venue: Greenation International Journal of Economics and Accounting
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of financial literacy on the financial performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), with social capital serving as a mediating variable in Jambi City, Indonesia. This research employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative analysis using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with qualitative insights from in-depth field interviews. The study sample comprises 395 MSME owners selected using Slovin's formula. The results reveal that financial literacy has a positive and significant effect on both financial performance and social capital. Furthermore, social capital significantly influences financial performance and mediates the relationship between financial literacy and MSME financial performance. These findings highlight that financial literacy is not merely a technical capability in managing finance but also a strategic competence in building trust, networks, and social collaboration that enhance business competitiveness. The novelty of this research lies in integrating cognitive and social dimensions into a single empirical model to explain MSME financial resilience. Practically, the findings provide strategic insights for policymakers and practitioners to design empowerment programs that enhance financial literacy and strengthen social capital, thereby improving MSME performance and sustainability amid global economic dynamics.

title: Improving Pesantren Performance Through Transformational Leadership, Social Entrepreneurship, and Social Capital: The Mediating Roles of Creativity and Social Value Creation
authors: Muhammad Hafidh Nashrullah; Sukesi; Slamet Riyadi; Nawari; Ahmad Munir Hamid
abstract: This study examines how transformational leadership, social entrepreneurship, and social capital influence pesantren performance, both directly and indirectly through creativity and social value creation. A quantitative explanatory design was applied using a census of 217 respondents, consisting of 9 leaders and 208 employees of pesantren business units from nine pesantren in East Java, Indonesia. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4.1. The structural model explained 61.2% of the variance in pesantren performance (R² = 0.612), 33.0% of the variance in social value creation (R² = 0.330), and 29.5% of the variance in creativity (R² = 0.295). The strongest direct effect was transformational leadership on social value creation (β = 0.424, p < 0.001), followed by social entrepreneurship on social value creation (β = 0.404, p < 0.001). Transformational leadership, social entrepreneurship, and social capital significantly increased creativity. Transformational leadership and social entrepreneurship also significantly increased social value creation, whereas social capital did not have a significant direct effect on social value creation (β = 0.075, p = 0.281). Pesantren performance was significantly influenced by transformational leadership, social entrepreneurship, social capital, creativity, and social value creation. Creativity significantly mediated the effects of transformational leadership (β = 0.072, p = 0.021), social entrepreneurship (β = 0.054, p = 0.033), and social capital (β = 0.065, p = 0.012) on pesantren performance. Social value creation mediated the effects of transformational leadership (β = 0.097, p = 0.001) and social entrepreneurship (β = 0.092, p = 0.004), but it did not mediate the relationship between social capital and performance (β = 0.017, p = 0.325). The findings show that pesantren performance is strengthened when leadership, entrepreneurial orientation, and relational resources are converted into creative organizational routines and measurable social value.

title: Associations of maternal uncertainty stress and social capital with adolescents’ smartphone use behavior: a cross-sectional study from rural China
authors: Xinxin Ying; Yanqi Li; Ruyu Sun; H J Zhou; Weifang Zhang
abstract: BACKGROUND: Smartphone use behavior among adolescents is a growing public health concern. Maternal uncertainty stress, defined as psychological stress arising from perceived unpredictability and uncontrollability in daily life and future circumstances, may contribute to these behaviors but remains understudied. While social capital can protect against adolescent risks, its role in maternal stress effects, particularly in rural areas, is unclear. This study examines the associations between maternal uncertainty stress, three dimensions of social capital, and adolescents' smartphone use behaviors in rural China. METHODS: A total of 1,215 adolescents (Mage = 13.38 ± 0.53 years, 52.4% males) and their mothers (Mage = 40.47 ± 4.80 years) were enrolled from five rural middle schools 7th grade in Zhejiang Province, China (2023). Data were collected through validated self-reported questionnaires. Multiple logistic regression models and structural equation modeling were used to explore the relationships between maternal uncertainty stress, social capital dimensions (social network, social participation, and cognitive social capital), and two domains of adolescents' smartphone use behavior: longer-duration use and non-study-related content engagement. RESULTS: Maternal uncertainty stress was significantly associated with adolescents' smartphone use behaviors, including longer-duration use and non-study-relate content engagement. Social capital, particularly cognitive social capital, played a bidirectional role as both a correlate of adolescent smartphone behaviors and a protective factor to mitigate the impact of maternal uncertainty stress. CONCLUSIONS: Maternal uncertainty stress and social capital are important factors influencing adolescents' smartphone use behaviors in rural China. Intervention programs aimed at reducing adolescent longer-duration and non-study use smartphone use should prioritize strengthening maternal social capital and providing effective coping strategies to manage uncertainty stress. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

title: SOCIOLOGICAL STUDY OF SCHOOLING, SOCIAL CAPITAL, AND CURRICULUM GAPS IN FOSTERING ENTREPRENEURIAL ASPIRATION AND ENTERPRISE CULTURE AMONG UNDERGRADUATES IN NORTHWEST, NIGERIA
authors: Aminu Musa Gusau; SADA AHMED JIBIA; TANIMU ADAM IBRAHIM
abstract: This study examined the role of schooling, social capital, and curriculum gaps in shaping This entrepreneurial aspirations and enterprise culture among undergraduates in Northwest Nigeria. It employed a descriptive survey design, involving 400 undergraduates from four public universities across Kano, Katsina, Sokoto, and Kaduna States, selected through a multi-stage stratified random sampling process. A structured questionnaire, validated by experts in curriculum studies and entrepreneurship education and subjected to a reliability test yielding a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of 0.81, was used for data collection. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and inferential statistics at the 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed that curriculum content in the sampled universities exhibits a moderate but insufficient integration of entrepreneurship-oriented learning experiences, that undergraduates' access to social capital (family networks, mentorship, and community ties) significantly predicts entrepreneurial aspiration, and that gaps between the formal curriculum and lived enterprise culture persist across disciplines and gender lines. The study concludes that curriculum reform alone, without deliberate attention to the sociological structures that mediate access to opportunity, is unlikely to produce a robust enterprise culture. Recommendations include embedding experiential entrepreneurship modules across all faculties, institutionalising structured mentorship and networking schemes, and mainstreaming sociological content on social capital into curriculum planning processes in Nigerian universities.

title: How Leader-Member Exchange Fosters Knowledge Sharing: A Dual-Pathway Model of Perceived Training Opportunities and Perceived Social Capital
authors: Tan Xi; Hyeran Choi
abstract: 본 연구는 리더-구성원 교환관계가 종업원의 개발적 자원 및 관계적 자원에 대한 지각을 통해 지 식공유를 어떠한 방식으로 촉진하는지를 규명하고자 하였다. 자원보존이론과 사회정체성 관점을 바 탕으로, 본 연구는 리더-구성원 교환관계가 지각된 훈련기회와 지각된 사회적 자본을 증진시키고, 이러한 자원이 다시 지식공유를 촉진하는 이중경로 모형을 제안하였다. 중국 소재 5개 인터넷 기업 에 재직 중인 종업원 626명을 대상으로 수집한 설문자료를 분석한 결과, 높은 수준의 리더-구성원 교환관계는 지각된 훈련기회 및 지각된 사회적 자본과 모두 유의한 정(+)의 관계를 가지는 것으로 나타났다. 또한 이러한 지각된 자원은 팀 구성원 간 지식공유를 유의하게 촉진하는 것으로 확인되었 다. 나아가 분석 결과는 리더-구성원 교환관계와 지식공유의 관계에서 지각된 훈련기회와 지각된 사회적 자본이 매개역할을 수행함을 지지하였다. 이는 리더십을 통해 형성된 자원이 종업원의 지각 을 매개로 협력적 행동으로 전환될 수 있음을 보여준다. 본 연구는 리더-구성원 교환관계가 종업원 이 지각하는 자원 가용성을 통해 어떻게 작동하는지를 구체화하고, 팀 맥락에서 자원전환 과정이 어떠한 방식으로 전개되는지를 설명함으로써 리더십 및 지식공유 연구에 이론적 기여를 제공한다. 실무적으로는 조직 내 지식공유를 강화하기 위해 종업원 개발에 대한 투자와 함께 사회적 연결 및 상호교환을 강화할 수 있는 협력적 환경 조성이 필요함을 시사한다.

title: The chain-mediating role of workplace social capital and resilience in the relationship between change fatigue and proactive work behavior among nurses
authors: 杨楠; Qing Tian; Lin Nie
abstract: Objective To examine the associations among change fatigue, workplace social capital, resilience, and proactive work behavior in clinical nurses, and to test whether workplace social capital and resilience serially mediate the relationship between change fatigue and proactive work behavior. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from January to April 2026. Convenience sampling was used to recruit 1,018 clinical nurses. Participants completed a demographic questionnaire, the Change Fatigue Scale, the Resilience Scale for Nurses, and the Proactive Work Behavior Scale. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and a saturated path model with 5,000 bootstrap samples (AMOS 25.0) were used. Results Nurses’ mean scores were 25.01 ± 7.97 for change fatigue, 77.50 ± 16.26 for workplace social capital, 63.80 ± 8.27 for resilience, and 31.78 ± 9.15 for proactive work behavior. Change fatigue was negatively correlated with workplace social capital, resilience, and proactive work behavior ( r = −0.447 to −0.738, all p < 0.001). Workplace social capital and resilience were each associated with partial mediation (specific indirect effects −0.173, 24.9%; −0.187, 26.9%), and the serial indirect effect was also significant (−0.075, 10.8%). The direct effect accounted for 37.3% of the total effect. The four-factor measurement model fitted better than a one-factor model, but absolute fit was poor (RMSEA = 0.111) and discriminant validity involving resilience was not supported. Conclusion Change fatigue is associated with lower proactive work behavior, and workplace social capital and resilience may partly explain this association. Monitoring change fatigue and fostering workplace social capital and resilience may support proactive work behavior; these propositions warrant longitudinal and intervention research.

title: How do firms use tacit knowledge in virtual brand communities to improve innovation performance? Based on virtual social capital perspective
authors: Jian Zheng; Xiaocui Li; Fen Wang; Cheng Wang; Yingzhen Chen
abstract: In the context of virtual brand communities (VBCs) and based on social capital theory, this study investigates the effect of each dimension of tacit knowledge (TK) on firm innovation performance (FIP) and the mechanism of the digital dimension of virtual social capital driving the improvement of FIP through the TK transmission chain. This study also examines the moderating effect of social media capability (SMC) on the relationship between TK and FIP. This study uses 647 samples collected from Chinese firms and employs the structural equation model and hierarchical regression analysis to conduct empirical tests. The three dimensions of TK have significant positive effects on FIP, among which skill-based tacit knowledge is the most notable. Network embeddedness has a significant positive effect on cognitive TK and social TK. Digital trust only has a significant positive effect on social TK. Sharing cognition has a significant positive effect on the three dimensions of TK. Social media proficiency has a positive moderating effect on the three dimensions of TK and FIP. Conversely, social media agility only has a positive moderating effect on social TK and FIP. This study tries to divide the dimensions of TK in VBCs, while also clarifying the function path of virtual social capital to improve FIP through TK. Additionally, it explores the moderating effect of SMC on OBL and FIP. This study’s findings provide theoretical support and practical inspiration for firms to use TK from VBCs to improve FIP.

title: Association between emotional intelligence and organizational commitment among clinical nurses: workplace social capital as a potential mediator in a cross-sectional study
authors: Linfei Ding; YE Qiaohua; Lihua Yu; Min Liao; Haixin Du; Yunxun Chen
abstract: Background Workplace social capital has been shown to alleviate occupational stress and enhance job wellbeing and satisfaction. However, limited research has examined the mediational pattern involving workplace social capital between EI and organizational commitment among clinical nurses. This study aims to investigate the indirect effect of EI on organizational commitment through workplace social capital, providing empirical evidence for nursing managers to develop strategies that may enhance nurses' organizational commitment. Methods A cross-sectional study design was adopted. A total of 648 clinical nurses from two tertiary and two secondary hospitals in Sichuan Province were recruited between June and November 2024 using a convenience cluster sampling approach. The research instruments included a general information questionnaire, the EI Scale, the Workplace Social Capital Scale, and the Organizational Commitment Scale. Descriptive statistics were performed using SPSS version 27.0, and structural equation modeling was conducted with AMOS version 24.0. Results EI showed a significant direct positive association with organizational commitment after controlling for workplace social capital (effect = 0.229, p < 0.001; bias-corrected 95% CI [0.126, 0.342]), accounting for 38.62% of the total effect. In addition, the indirect association between EI and organizational commitment through workplace social capital was statistically significant (effect = 0.364, p < 0.001; bias-corrected 95% CI [0.295, 0.444]), accounting for 61.38% of the total effect. These findings are consistent with a partial mediation model. Conclusion The findings of this cross-sectional study suggest that workplace social capital is an important intervening variable in the relationship between EI and organizational commitment among clinical nurses, with the indirect effect accounting for a larger proportion of the total effect than the direct effect. These results provide empirical support for the hypothesized mediating model, though causal conclusions require longitudinal or experimental validation.

title: The Effects of Park Golf Participation Characteristics on Quality of Life and Social Isolation among Older Adults : Focusing on the Mediating Effect of Social Capital
authors: 경희대학교; Sun-Hee Kim; Min-Ah Ryu; Il-Han Seo
abstract: [목적] 본 연구는 파크골프 참여특성이 고령층의 삶의 질과 사회적 고립에 미치는 영향을 규명하는 데 목적이 있다. [방법] 서울 및 수도권 파크골프장 이용 고령층을 대상으로 설문조사 하였고, 최종 411부를 분석하였다. 자료는 SPSS 29.0과 AMOS 29.0을 이용해 CFA와 SEM으로 분석하였다. [결과] 첫째, 파크골프 참여특성은 사회적 자본에 유의한 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤다. 둘째, 사회적 자본은 삶의 질에 정(+)의 영향을, 사회적 고립에는 부(-)의 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 셋째, 참여특성은 삶의 질에는 직접적인 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤으나 사회적 고립에는 유의한 영향을 미치지 않았다. 넷째, 사회적 자본은 참여특성과 삶의 질 간에는 부분매개, 참여특성과 사회적 고립 간에는 완전매개 역할을 수행하는 것으로 확인되었다. [결론] 파크골프 참여는 고령층의 삶의 질을 향상시키고 사회적 고립을 완화하며, 이러한 효과는 사회적 자본 형성을 통해 더욱 강화되는 것으로 나타났다.

title: Major differences in the relationship between electronic health literacy, social capital and negative mental health states among the university students in China
authors: Zhengna Sun; Rui Chen; Mao Cheng; Kaiyuan Feng; Qinling Li; Ziwei Qin
abstract: Abstract Background The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between electronic health literacy (eHealth literacy), social capital and negative mental health statesamong Chinese university students, and further clarify its major disparities. Methods The data was gathered from Chinese university students via Wenjuan.com using the snowball sampling method. Data from 1472 participants were analyzed, with 665 (45.18%) medical students (MS) and 807 (54.82%) non-medical students (NMS). Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21) was utilized to assess negative mental health states, eHealth Literacy Scale (eHEALS) to measure eHealth literacy, and Chinese Shortened Social Capital Scale (CSSCS) to evaluate social capital. To explore the relationships among eHealth literacy, social capital and negative mental health states, SPSS was used for descriptive analysis, chi-square tests and t-tests, and AMOS was used for structural equation modeling (SEM). Results Total scores of negative mental health states was 30.87 ± 26.72 (25.26 ± 24.86 for MS, 35.49 ± 27.33 for NMS). eHealth literacy was significantly positively associated with negative mental health states in MS but not significant among NMS. Social capital was negatively associated with negative mental health states among MS and NMS. eHealth literacy showed a significant positive association with social capital among MS and NMS.
